The Gospel According to Matthew

Wheel of Heaven Translation

Eight canon-cited chapters from the earliest substantial Koine Greek manuscript witnesses: Mt 1 (genealogy + virgin birth); Mt 5-7 (Sermon on the Mount); Mt 13 (kingdom parables); Mt 17 (Transfiguration); Mt 25 (final judgment); Mt 28 (Resurrection + Great Commission)

Direct Direct Established or uncontested across mainstream sources, or a direct description of the project itself. Framework Framework Foundational premise of the Wheel of Heaven framework. Explicit in the Raëlian canon; not endorsed by mainstream scholarship. Inferred Inferred A reasonable reading of comparative material — not stated literally, but consistent with the source. Speculative Speculative Interpretive synthesis or hypothesis that goes beyond what any single source states.

An English translation of the eight Matthew chapters most heavily engaged by the Raëlian canon — produced from the earliest substantial Koine Greek manuscript witnesses (4th c. CE uncials Vaticanus and Sinaiticus, cross-collated against the 2nd-3rd c. CE papyri P45, P64+P67, P77, P103, P104). **The project's first Christian-tradition text** and **first Koine Greek source text**. The 8 canon-cited chapters: **Mt 1** (genealogy of Jesus + the virgin-birth narrative); **Mt 5** (Sermon on the Mount Pt I: Beatitudes, salt and light, 'not to abolish but to fulfill,' the antitheses); **Mt 6** (Sermon on the Mount Pt II: alms, the Lord's Prayer, fasting, treasure in heaven, anxiety); **Mt 7** (Sermon on the Mount Pt III: judgment, ask-seek-knock, the golden rule, the narrow gate, the two builders); **Mt 13** (the kingdom parables — the Parable of the Sower is **the canon's explicit panspermia-citation site** per Raël's reading as 'life being seeded on multiple worlds'); **Mt 17** (the Transfiguration + the demoniac boy + the temple-tax); **Mt 25** (Ten Virgins + Talents + Sheep and Goats — the final-judgment chapter); **Mt 28** (the Resurrection + the Great Commission). The **early-manuscript approach** parallels the Qur'an translation's Tübingen Ma VI 165 + Codex Parisino-petropolitanus method: source the text from the earliest substantially-complete codices (Vaticanus 4th c., Sinaiticus 4th c.), cross-collate against the earlier papyri where they preserve target verses (P104 ~150 CE is among the earliest witnesses to Matthew — earlier than both uncials by ~150-200 years), and document NA28/UBS5/SBLGNT critical-apparatus variants per verse. **Fourth canon-source-tension closure** after Shi'ur Qomah (*parasangs*), Qur'an (*inshiqāq al-qamar* + *ḥūr ʿīn*), and Exodus (pillar/parting/manna/theophany). The acknowledgment-without-endorsement framework is applied at the Mt 13 Parable-of-the-Sower panspermia-site + Mt 17 Transfiguration + Mt 28 Resurrection + Great Commission canon-engagement sites — same pattern. The WoH-Translation produces the philologically-disciplined version with explicit operational disavowals against (a) the Raëlian-canon Mt 13 panspermia pre-resolution; (b) Christian-supersessionist readings (Mt 5:17 'not to abolish but to fulfill' must NOT be theologized into 'Old-Testament-superseded'); (c) the Isa 7:14 LXX-*parthenos* vs Hebrew *ʿalmâ* virgin-birth philological dispute preserved-not-adjudicated; (d) Sitchin/Anunnaki-engineered-spiritual-technology pre-resolution; (e) the orientalist/colonialist Great-Commission misreadings.

Chapter 1

Matthew 1 — Genealogy of Jesus + the virgin-birth narrative

1
The book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, son of David, son of Abraham.
The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.
Βίβλος γενέσεως Ἰησοῦ χριστοῦ υἱοῦ Δαυὶδ υἱοῦ Ἀβραάμ.
Translation Commentary Verse 1

Biblos geneseōs — the genealogical incipit deliberately calques Gen 2:4 LXX / Gen 5:1 LXX biblos geneseōs (itself rendering Hebrew sēfer tôlĕdôt 'book of generations'). The Matthean opening positions the gospel as a new Genesis, framing the Jesus-narrative as a creation-typological event in Hebrew Bible-cosmological register. Iēsou christou deploys the Greek-Hebrew-Aramaic cognate trio (see glossary christos-māšîaḥ-anointed-one-cross-corpus-greek-hebrew-aramaic and iēsous-yehoshua-yhwh-saves-folk-etymology-cross-corpus). Davies-Allison ICC 1.149-160; Brown 1993 64-95; Luz Hermeneia 1.81-86.

2
Abraham begot Isaac, and Isaac begot Jacob, and Jacob begot Judah and his brothers,
Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat Judah and his brethren;
Ἀβραὰμ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰσαάκ, Ἰσαὰκ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰακώβ, Ἰακὼβ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰούδαν καὶ τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοῦ,
3
and Judah begot Perez and Zerah by Tamar, and Perez begot Hezron, and Hezron begot Aram,
and Judah begat Perez and Zerah of Tamar; and Perez begat Hezron; and Hezron begat Ram;
Ἰούδας δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Φαρὲς καὶ τὸν Ζαρὰ ἐκ τῆς Θαμάρ, Φαρὲς δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἑσρώμ, Ἑσρὼμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀράμ,
Translation Commentary Verse 3

Tamar is the first of four women named in the Matthean genealogy (Tamar / Rahab / Ruth / wife-of-Uriah, plus Mary at v.16). Davies-Allison ICC 1.170-172 list four interpretive readings of the inclusion: (a) the women as sinners (foregrounding divine-grace in irregular-genealogy); (b) the women as foreigners (foregrounding Gentile-inclusion in the Davidic-line); (c) the women as marked by irregular-sexual-unions (preparing the reader for Mary's irregular-conception); (d) divine-providence-through-irregularity (the Davidic-line preserved through divine-initiative). The fourth reading is the modern critical consensus (Brown 1993 73-74; Luz Hermeneia 1.85). The text preserves all four readings without surface-adjudication.

4
and Aram begot Amminadab, and Amminadab begot Nahshon, and Nahshon begot Salmon,
and Ram begat Amminadab; and Amminadab begat Nahshon; and Nahshon begat Salmon;
Ἀρὰμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀμιναδάβ, Ἀμιναδὰβ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ναασσών, Ναασσὼν δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Σαλμών,
5
and Salmon begot Boaz by Rahab, and Boaz begot Obed by Ruth, and Obed begot Jesse,
and Salmon begat Boaz of Rahab; and Boaz begat Obed of Ruth; and Obed begat Jesse;
Σαλμὼν δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Βοὲς ἐκ τῆς Ῥαχάβ, Βοὲς δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωβὴδ ἐκ τῆς Ῥούθ, Ἰωβὴδ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰεσσαί,
6
and Jesse begot David the king. And David begot Solomon by the wife of Uriah,
and Jesse begat David the king. And David begat Solomon of her [that had been the wife] of Uriah;
Ἰεσσαὶ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Δαυὶδ τὸν βασιλέα. Δαυὶδ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Σολομῶνα ἐκ τῆς τοῦ Οὐρίου,
Translation Commentary Verse 6

tēs tou Ouriou — the periphrastic feminine 'her of Uriah' (literally 'the [wife] of Uriah') deliberately AVOIDS naming Bathsheba directly. The naming-by-husband foregrounds the irregular-union (David's appropriation of Uriah's wife per 2 Sam 11) rather than the Bathsheba-figure herself. The Matthean rhetorical strategy preserves the moral-difficulty of the Davidic-line's foundational-irregularity. Davies-Allison ICC 1.174; Brown 1993 75-76; Luz Hermeneia 1.85.

7
and Solomon begot Rehoboam, and Rehoboam begot Abijah, and Abijah begot Asaph,
and Solomon begat Rehoboam; and Rehoboam begat Abijah; and Abijah begat Asa;
Σολομὼν δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ῥοβοάμ, Ῥοβοὰμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀβιά, Ἀβιὰ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀσάφ,
Translation Commentary Verse 7

Textual variant. Vaticanus (B/03) + Sinaiticus (א/01) + NA28/SBLGNT/THGNT critical text read Asaph (the psalmist's name); the Hebrew Bible 1 Chr 3:10 has ʾāsāʾ (Asa, the Judahite king). The Byzantine majority text + KJV harmonize to 'Asa'. The critical-text Asaph is widely-treated as either (a) a Matthean error / variant-source-list (Metzger 1994); (b) a deliberate-typological allusion to the psalmist (Davies-Allison ICC 1.176). The WoH-Translation preserves the critical-text Asaph.

8
and Asaph begot Jehoshaphat, and Jehoshaphat begot Joram, and Joram begot Uzziah,
and Asa begat Jehoshaphat; and Jehoshaphat begat Joram; and Joram begat Uzziah;
Ἀσὰφ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωσαφάτ, Ἰωσαφὰτ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωράμ, Ἰωρὰμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ὀζίαν,
9
and Uzziah begot Jotham, and Jotham begot Ahaz, and Ahaz begot Hezekiah,
and Uzziah begat Jotham; and Jotham begat Ahaz; and Ahaz begat Hezekiah;
Ὀζίας δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωαθάμ, Ἰωαθὰμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀχάζ, Ἀχὰζ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἑζεκίαν,
10
and Hezekiah begot Manasseh, and Manasseh begot Amos, and Amos begot Josiah,
and Hezekiah begat Manasseh; and Manasseh begat Amon; and Amon begat Josiah;
Ἑζεκίας δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Μανασσῆ, Μανασσῆς δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀμώς, Ἀμὼς δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωσίαν,
Translation Commentary Verse 10

Textual variant — parallel to v.7. Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + critical text read Amos (the prophet's name); the Hebrew Bible 2 Kgs 21:18 has ʾāmôn (Amon, the Judahite king). The Byzantine majority + KJV harmonize. Either a variant-source-list / Matthean error or a deliberate-typological allusion to the prophet. Metzger 1994; Davies-Allison ICC 1.177-178.

11
and Josiah begot Jechoniah and his brothers, at the time of the deportation to Babylon.
and Josiah begat Jechoniah and his brethren, at the time of the carrying away to Babylon.
Ἰωσίας δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰεχονίαν καὶ τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τῆς μετοικεσίας Βαβυλῶνος.
12
And after the deportation to Babylon, Jechoniah begot Salathiel, and Salathiel begot Zerubbabel,
And after the carrying away to Babylon, Jechoniah begat Shealtiel; and Shealtiel begat Zerubbabel;
Μετὰ δὲ τὴν μετοικεσίαν Βαβυλῶνος Ἰεχονίας ἐγέννησεν τὸν Σαλαθιήλ, Σαλαθιὴλ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ζοροβαβέλ,
13
and Zerubbabel begot Abiud, and Abiud begot Eliakim, and Eliakim begot Azor,
and Zerubbabel begat Abiud; and Abiud begat Eliakim; and Eliakim begat Azor;
Ζοροβαβὲλ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀβιούδ, Ἀβιοὺδ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἐλιακίμ, Ἐλιακὶμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀζώρ,
14
and Azor begot Zadok, and Zadok begot Achim, and Achim begot Eliud,
and Azor begat Sadoc; and Sadoc begat Achim; and Achim begat Eliud;
Ἀζὼρ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Σαδώκ, Σαδὼκ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀχίμ, Ἀχὶμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἐλιούδ,
15
and Eliud begot Eleazar, and Eleazar begot Matthan, and Matthan begot Jacob,
and Eliud begat Eleazar; and Eleazar begat Matthan; and Matthan begat Jacob;
Ἐλιοὺδ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἐλεάζαρ, Ἐλεάζαρ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ματθάν, Ματθὰν δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰακώβ,
16
and Jacob begot Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.
and Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.
Ἰακὼβ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωσὴφ τὸν ἄνδρα Μαρίας, ἐξ ἧς ἐγεννήθη Ἰησοῦς ὁ λεγόμενος χριστός.
Translation Commentary Verse 16

ex hēs egennēthē — the genealogical break: feminine relative hēs 'of whom' (referring to Mary, not Joseph) and the passive egennēthē 'was born' both signal the virgin-conception. The Matthean grammar breaks the otherwise-active masculine-begetting pattern of the genealogy. A small group of witnesses (Sinaitic Syriac, some Old Latin) reads 'Joseph begot Jesus' — generally rejected as harmonizing-adoptionist. Davies-Allison ICC 1.183-184; Brown 1993 138-139.

17
So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations, and from David to the deportation to Babylon fourteen generations, and from the deportation to Babylon to the Christ fourteen generations.
So all the generations from Abraham unto David are fourteen generations; and from David unto the carrying away to Babylon fourteen generations; and from the carrying away to Babylon unto the Christ fourteen generations.
Πᾶσαι οὖν αἱ γενεαὶ ἀπὸ Ἀβραὰμ ἕως Δαυὶδ γενεαὶ δεκατέσσαρες, καὶ ἀπὸ Δαυὶδ ἕως τῆς μετοικεσίας Βαβυλῶνος γενεαὶ δεκατέσσαρες, καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς μετοικεσίας Βαβυλῶνος ἕως τοῦ χριστοῦ γενεαὶ δεκατέσσαρες.
Translation Commentary Verse 17

Schematic 14×3 generation-pattern. 14 = 2×7 (sevenfold-completion doubled); 14 also equals the gematria of DWD = דוד (D=4 + W=6 + D=4 = 14), David's name. The strict arithmetic counts 14+14+13 names (third section missing one), so the schema is interpretive-intent over strict-arithmetic. The triple-fourteen structures the Davidic-line and positions the Messiah at the 3×14 = 42 = 6×7 climax of the typological-schema. Davies-Allison ICC 1.161-165; Brown 1993 74-84.

18
Now the birth of Jesus Christ was in this way. When his mother Mary had been betrothed to Joseph, before they came together she was found to be with child of the Holy Spirit.
Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When his mother Mary had been betrothed to Joseph, before they came together she was found with child of the Holy Spirit.
Τοῦ δὲ Ἰησοῦ χριστοῦ ἡ γένεσις οὕτως ἦν. μνηστευθείσης τῆς μητρὸς αὐτοῦ Μαρίας τῷ Ἰωσήφ, πρὶν ἢ συνελθεῖν αὐτοὺς εὑρέθη ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχουσα ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου.
Translation Commentary Verse 18

ek pneumatos hagiou — 'of [a] holy spirit' (anarthrous). The Greek lacks the definite article, which in 1st-c. usage does NOT yet carry the fully-developed Trinitarian Holy-Spirit-as-third-person sense (a 4th-c. theological development). Brown 1993 124-125 cautions against retrojecting Nicene Trinitarian theology onto the 1st-c. anarthrous phrase. Davies-Allison ICC 1.200-203 treat the conception-narrative against the OT divine-conception background (Gen 18 Sarah; 1 Sam 1 Hannah — but the Matthean ek pneumatos hagiou has no direct Hebrew Bible parallel for human-virginal-conception). The lens-risk site is preserved without surface-pre-resolution.

19
And Joseph her husband, being a righteous man and not wishing to expose her to disgrace, resolved to divorce her quietly.
And Joseph her husband, being a righteous man, and not willing to make her a public example, was minded to put her away privily.
Ἰωσὴφ δὲ ὁ ἀνὴρ αὐτῆς, δίκαιος ὢν καὶ μὴ θέλων αὐτὴν δειγματίσαι, ἐβουλήθη λάθρᾳ ἀπολῦσαι αὐτήν.
Translation Commentary Verse 19

dikaios ōn — the Matthean characterization of Joseph as 'righteous'. Two interpretive readings: (a) Joseph is law-observant (Deut 22:23-24 prescribes the death-penalty for adultery), and so obliged-to-divorce, but compassionately; (b) Joseph is righteous-as-merciful and refuses to expose Mary publicly. Both readings have ancient and modern defenders. Davies-Allison ICC 1.202-204; Brown 1993 125-128. The translation preserves the ambiguity.

20
But while he was considering these things, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying: "Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife, for that which has been conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit.
But when he thought on these things, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit.
ταῦτα δὲ αὐτοῦ ἐνθυμηθέντος ἰδοὺ ἄγγελος κυρίου κατ' ὄναρ ἐφάνη αὐτῷ λέγων· Ἰωσὴφ υἱὸς Δαυίδ, μὴ φοβηθῇς παραλαβεῖν Μαρίαν τὴν γυναῖκά σου, τὸ γὰρ ἐν αὐτῇ γεννηθὲν ἐκ πνεύματός ἐστιν ἁγίου·
Translation Commentary Verse 20

angelos kyriou kat' onar — the dream-vision angelophany. The phrase angelos kyriou directly calques the LXX rendering of malʾakh YHWH (the messenger-of-YHWH), the recurring Hebrew Bible theophanic-figure (Gen 16:7; Ex 3:2; Judg 13). The first of Joseph's four dream-revelations in Matthew (1:20; 2:13; 2:19; 2:22) — a Matthean Joseph-typological pattern echoing the Genesis Joseph (Gen 37 + 40-41) who likewise receives revelation through dreams. Davies-Allison ICC 1.204-207.

21
She will bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins."
And she shall bring forth a son; and thou shalt call his name JESUS; for it is he that shall save his people from their sins.
τέξεται δὲ υἱὸν καὶ καλέσεις τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦν, αὐτὸς γὰρ σώσει τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν.
Translation Commentary Verse 21

In-verse folk-etymology. Iēsoun ... sōsei — the Greek wordplay implicit (both -s-words); the Hebrew wordplay direct: Yēšûaʿ (Jesus) from root yšʿ 'to save' + the Yāh-theophoric → 'YHWH saves'. The angel-of-the-Lord explicitly invokes the yšʿ-element of the name as rationale for the naming. The closest typological-pattern is Sir 46:1 (the post-exilic Hebrew Sirach on Joshua-son-of-Nun: gibbôr ba-milḥāmâ ... le-hôšîaʿ ʾet bĕḥîrāyw 'a warrior in battle ... to save his chosen'). Davies-Allison ICC 1.209; Brown 1993 130-131.

22
Now all this took place so that what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying:
Now all this is come to pass, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Lord through the prophet, saying,
τοῦτο δὲ ὅλον γέγονεν ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν ὑπὸ κυρίου διὰ τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος·
Translation Commentary Verse 22

hina plērōthē — the first of Matthew's signature fulfillment-formulae (occurring 12x: Mt 1:22; 2:15; 2:17-18; 2:23; 4:14-16; 8:17; 12:17-21; 13:14-15; 13:35; 21:4-5; 27:9-10). The formula explicitly frames the Gospel as eschatological-fulfillment of Israel's scriptures. The semantic breadth of plēroō (cf. central entry abolish-or-fulfill-mt-5-17-katalysai-vs-plērōsai-christian-supersessionism-disavowal-cross-corpus) supports both 'fulfill prophecy' and 'bring to true-meaning fullness'. Davies-Allison ICC 1.209-213.

23
"Behold, the virgin shall be with child and shall bear a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel" — which is translated, "God with us."
Behold, the virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, And they shall call his name Immanuel; which is, being interpreted, God with us.
Ἰδοὺ ἡ παρθένος ἐν γαστρὶ ἕξει καὶ τέξεται υἱόν, καὶ καλέσουσιν τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἐμμανουήλ· ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον Μεθ' ἡμῶν ὁ θεός.
Translation Commentary Verse 23

Major philological crux: Isa 7:14 LXX parthenos vs Hebrew ʿalmâ. Matthew cites the LXX parthenos 'virgin'; the Hebrew MT reads ʿalmâ 'young woman of marriageable age' (technical Hebrew virgin = bĕtûlâ). The Isa 7:14 oracle in its 8th-c. BCE setting addresses King Ahaz during the Syro-Ephraimite crisis; the immediate-historical referent (wife of Ahaz / Isaiah / Davidic-house figure) is debated. The Jewish-Christian philological dispute dates to Justin Martyr's Dialogue with Trypho 71-77 (c. 155-160 CE). The WoH-Translation preserves the LXX-text Matthew cites without adjudicating the underlying Hebrew dispute — see isa-7-14-virgin-birth-mt-1-22-23-parthenos-vs-almah-philological-dispute-cross-corpus.

Emmanouēl ... Meth' hēmōn ho theos — the Matthean calque of Hebrew ʿimmānû-ʾēl 'with-us is El'. The Emmanuel-naming opens the Matthean structural-inclusio that closes at Mt 28:20 meth' hymōn eimi 'I am with you' — D. D. Kupp, Matthew's Emmanuel (SNTSMS 90, Cambridge 1996), the comprehensive monograph. See emmanuel-frame-inclusio-mt-1-23-mt-28-20-divine-presence-cross-corpus-kupp.

24
And Joseph, rising from sleep, did as the angel of the Lord had commanded him, and took his wife,
And Joseph arose from his sleep, and did as the angel of the Lord commanded him, and took unto him his wife;
ἐγερθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰωσὴφ ἀπὸ τοῦ ὕπνου ἐποίησεν ὡς προσέταξεν αὐτῷ ὁ ἄγγελος κυρίου καὶ παρέλαβεν τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ·
25
and did not know her until she had borne a son; and he called his name Jesus.
and knew her not till she had brought forth a son: and he called his name JESUS.
καὶ οὐκ ἐγίνωσκεν αὐτὴν ἕως οὗ ἔτεκεν υἱόν· καὶ ἐκάλεσεν τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦν.
Translation Commentary Verse 25

ouk eginōsken autēn heōs hou eteken huion — the imperfect eginōsken + heōs 'until' construction. The Catholic-Orthodox perpetual-virginity tradition reads heōs as terminating-no-implication (i.e., the relationship-status before-the-birth is asserted; what happens after is not implied); the Protestant tradition reads heōs as terminating-with-implication (i.e., the relationship-status changes after the birth). The Greek admits both readings; cf. Mt 28:20 meth' hymōn eimi pasas tas hēmeras heōs tēs synteleias tou aiōnos where heōs clearly does NOT imply termination. Textual variant: some Byzantine MSS add ton prōtotokon 'the firstborn' (KJV); absent in B + א + critical text. Davies-Allison ICC 1.218-219; Brown 1993 132-134.

Chapter 5

Matthew 5 — Sermon on the Mount Pt I: Beatitudes, salt and light, 'not to abolish but to fulfill,' the antitheses

1
And seeing the crowds, he went up onto the mountain; and when he had sat down, his disciples came to him.
Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judaea in the days of Herod the king, behold, Wise-men from the east came to Jerusalem, saying,
Ἰδὼν δὲ τοὺς ὄχλους ἀνέβη εἰς τὸ ὄρος· καὶ καθίσαντος αὐτοῦ προσῆλθαν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ·
Translation Commentary Verse 1

anebē eis to oros — Jesus 'went up onto the mountain'. The Matthean mountain-setting opens the structural-theological pattern of mountain-as-revelation-site that recurs at Mt 17:1 (Transfiguration) and Mt 28:16 (Great Commission). D. C. Allison, The New Moses (Fortress 1993), treats the Sermon-on-the-Mount mountain as Matthean Moses-typology — Jesus teaches Torah on the mountain, parallel to Moses on Sinai (Ex 19-20). See mountain-as-revelation-site-mt-cross-corpus-har-sinai-mount-sapunu.

2
And opening his mouth, he taught them, saying:
Where is he that is born King of the Jews? for we saw his star in the east, and are come to worship him.
καὶ ἀνοίξας τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτοὺς λέγων·
3
Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of the heavens.
And when Herod the king heard it, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.
Μακάριοι οἱ πτωχοὶ τῷ πνεύματι, ὅτι αὐτῶν ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.
Translation Commentary Verse 3

Makarioi hoi ptōchoi tō pneumati — the first beatitude. makarios (LXX-Greek standardly rendering Hebrew ʾašrê) opens the Hebrew wisdom-beatitude tradition (Ps 1:1; 32:1; 119:1-2). The Matthean tō pneumati spiritualization (vs the Lukan ptōchoi simple-poverty at Lk 6:20) likely reflects an Aramaic-Hebrew ʿănāwîm / 1QM 11:9 ʿnwy rwḥ 'humble-of-spirit' Qumran-community background. basileia tōn ouranōn — the Matthean-distinctive rabbinic-malkhut shamayim-style circumlocution; see beatitudes-mt-5-3-12-makarios-formula-ethical-teaching-cross-corpus and kingdom-of-heaven-basileia-tōn-ouranōn-mt-distinctive-cross-corpus-hebrew-malkhut-shamayim.

4
Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted.
And gathering together all the chief priests and scribes of the people, he inquired of them where the Christ should be born.
μακάριοι οἱ πενθοῦντες, ὅτι αὐτοὶ παρακληθήσονται.
Translation Commentary Verse 4

makarioi hoi penthountes — the mourners-beatitude. Direct LXX-citation of Isa 61:2 parakalesai pantas tous penthountas 'to comfort all who mourn'. The Matthean Jesus opens the SM with the Isa 61 Servant-of-YHWH program — the proclamation of liberation to the brokenhearted. Davies-Allison ICC 1.448-449.

5
Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth.
And they said unto him, In Bethlehem of Judaea: for thus it is written through the prophet,
μακάριοι οἱ πραεῖς, ὅτι αὐτοὶ κληρονομήσουσιν τὴν γῆν.
Translation Commentary Verse 5

makarioi hoi praeis ... klēronomēsousin tēn gēn — direct LXX-citation of Ps 37:11 praeis ... klēronomēsousin gēn 'the meek shall inherit the land'. The gē admits both 'earth' (cosmic) and 'land' (Israelite-territorial). The Hebrew ʾereṣ at Ps 37:11 has both senses; the Matthean gē preserves the ambiguity. Davies-Allison ICC 1.449-451.

6
Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be filled.
And thou Bethlehem, land of Judah, Art in no wise least among the princes of Judah: For out of thee shall come forth a governor, Who shall be shepherd of my people Israel.
μακάριοι οἱ πεινῶντες καὶ διψῶντες τὴν δικαιοσύνην, ὅτι αὐτοὶ χορτασθήσονται.
Translation Commentary Verse 6

peinōntes kai dipsōntes tēn dikaiosynēn — hunger-and-thirst-for-righteousness. The wisdom-tradition hunger-for-wisdom motif (Prov 9:5; Sir 24:21; Wisdom 7:7); also echoes Isa 55:1-2 (the prophetic invitation to drink-without-cost). The Matthean dikaiosynē covers both forensic-righteousness and ethical-justice-doing; the philological breadth is preserved.

7
Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy.
Then Herod privily called the Wise-men, and learned of them exactly what time the star appeared.
μακάριοι οἱ ἐλεήμονες, ὅτι αὐτοὶ ἐλεηθήσονται.
8
Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.
And he sent them to Bethlehem, and said, Go and search out exactly concerning the young child; and when ye have found [him,] bring me word, that I also may come and worship him.
μακάριοι οἱ καθαροὶ τῇ καρδίᾳ, ὅτι αὐτοὶ τὸν θεὸν ὄψονται.
Translation Commentary Verse 8

katharoi tē kardia ... ton theon opsontai — pure-in-heart shall-see-God. Direct LXX-citation of Ps 24:4 kathar tē kardia. The promise ton theon opsontai sits in tension with the Ex 33:20 'no one can see God and live' tradition; the prophetic seeing-YHWH tradition (Isa 6:1-5; Ezek 1; Dan 7) is the cross-corpus background. The beatific-vision theological tradition derives substantially from this verse + Heb 12:14. Davies-Allison ICC 1.456-457.

9
Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons of God.
And they, having heard the king, went their way; and lo, the star, which they saw in the east, went before them, till it came and stood over where the young child was.
μακάριοι οἱ εἰρηνοποιοί, ὅτι αὐτοὶ υἱοὶ θεοῦ κληθήσονται.
10
Blessed are those who have been persecuted for righteousness' sake, for theirs is the kingdom of the heavens.
And when they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceeding great joy.
μακάριοι οἱ δεδιωγμένοι ἕνεκεν δικαιοσύνης, ὅτι αὐτῶν ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.
Translation Commentary Verse 10

hoi dediōgmenoi heneken dikaiosynēs ... basileia tōn ouranōn — the eighth beatitude closes the eight-beatitude structural-pattern with the inclusio repetition of the kingdom-promise from v.3 (theirs is the kingdom of the heavens). Davies-Allison ICC 1.459-462.

11
Blessed are you when they revile you and persecute you and speak every kind of evil against you, lying, on my account.
And they came into the house and saw the young child with Mary his mother; and they fell down and worshipped him; and opening their treasures they offered unto him gifts, gold and frankincense and myrrh.
μακάριοί ἐστε ὅταν ὀνειδίσωσιν ὑμᾶς καὶ διώξωσιν καὶ εἴπωσιν πᾶν πονηρὸν καθ' ὑμῶν ψευδόμενοι ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ·
Translation Commentary Verse 11

The expanded ninth beatitude (vv.11-12) shifts to direct-address (hymeis) and breaks the third-person pattern. Generally treated as a Matthean expansion of the original eight-beatitude unit, addressing the situation of the Matthean community under persecution. Davies-Allison ICC 1.464-467.

12
Rejoice and be glad, for your reward in the heavens is great; for so they persecuted the prophets who were before you.
And being warned [of God] in a dream that they should not return to Herod, they departed into their own country another way.
χαίρετε καὶ ἀγαλλιᾶσθε, ὅτι ὁ μισθὸς ὑμῶν πολὺς ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς· οὕτως γὰρ ἐδίωξαν τοὺς προφήτας τοὺς πρὸ ὑμῶν.
13
You are the salt of the earth; but if the salt has lost its savor, with what shall it be salted? It is no longer good for anything, except to be thrown out and trodden underfoot by people.
Now when they were departed, behold, an angel of the Lord appeareth to Joseph in a dream, saying, Arise and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and be thou there until I tell thee: for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him.
Ὑμεῖς ἐστε τὸ ἅλας τῆς γῆς· ἐὰν δὲ τὸ ἅλας μωρανθῇ, ἐν τίνι ἁλισθήσεται; εἰς οὐδὲν ἰσχύει ἔτι εἰ μὴ βληθὲν ἔξω καταπατεῖσθαι ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων.
14
You are the light of the world. A city set on a hill cannot be hidden.
And he arose and took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt;
Ὑμεῖς ἐστε τὸ φῶς τοῦ κόσμου. οὐ δύναται πόλις κρυβῆναι ἐπάνω ὄρους κειμένη·
Translation Commentary Verse 14

hē polis ... epanō orous keimenē — 'a city set upon a mountain'. Possible echoes: Isa 2:2-3 / Mic 4:1-2 (the eschatological-Zion drawing all nations to the mountain-of-YHWH); the Sermon-on-the-Mount mountain itself. The Matthean structural-pattern of mountain-as-revelation-site is operative. See mountain-as-revelation-site-mt-cross-corpus-har-sinai-mount-sapunu.

15
Nor do they light a lamp and put it under a basket, but on a lampstand, and it gives light to all who are in the house.
and was there until the death of Herod: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Lord through the prophet, saying, Out of Egypt did I call my son.
οὐδὲ καίουσιν λύχνον καὶ τιθέασιν αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τὸν μόδιον ἀλλ' ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν, καὶ λάμπει πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ.
16
Even so, let your light shine before people, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father who is in the heavens.
Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked of the Wise-men, was exceeding wroth, and sent forth, and slew all the male children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the borders thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had exactly learned of the Wise-men.
οὕτως λαμψάτω τὸ φῶς ὑμῶν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὅπως ἴδωσιν ὑμῶν τὰ καλὰ ἔργα καὶ δοξάσωσιν τὸν πατέρα ὑμῶν τὸν ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.
17
Do not think that I came to abolish the Law or the Prophets; I did not come to abolish, but to fulfill.
Then was fulfilled that which was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet, saying,
Μὴ νομίσητε ὅτι ἦλθον καταλῦσαι τὸν νόμον ἢ τοὺς προφήτας· οὐκ ἦλθον καταλῦσαι ἀλλὰ πληρῶσαι·
Translation Commentary Verse 17

The central Matthean Torah-stance statement. Mē nomisēte hoti ēlthon katalysai ... ouk ēlthon katalysai alla plērōsai — 'do not think I came to abolish ... I came to fulfill'. The verb-pair katalysai (abolish) vs plērōsai (fulfill / fill-to-fullness) carries the entire weight of the Matthean Torah-stance. The Matthean Jesus explicitly disavows Torah-abrogation; the antitheses that follow (vv.21-48) are intensifications, not replacements. The Christian-supersessionist reading (Marcionite tendencies; Reformation law-vs-grace; dispensationalism) is a downstream 2nd-c.-and-later development that the Matthean text resists. See abolish-or-fulfill-mt-5-17-katalysai-vs-plērōsai-christian-supersessionism-disavowal-cross-corpus.

18
For amen I say to you: until heaven and earth pass away, not one iota or one stroke shall pass away from the Law, until all is accomplished.
A voice was heard in Ramah, Weeping and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children; And she would not be comforted, because they are not.
ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν, ἕως ἂν παρέλθῃ ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ, ἰῶτα ἓν ἢ μία κεραία οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου, ἕως ἂν πάντα γένηται.
Translation Commentary Verse 18

amēn legō hymin — the Matthean Aramaic-loan amēn preserved untranslated, marking solemn-declaration. iōta hen ē mia keraia 'one yota or one stroke' — the smallest Hebrew letter (yod) and the smallest scribal mark (keraia). The Matthean Jesus' Torah-preservation-statement is explicit and uncompromising. Davies-Allison ICC 1.488-495.

19
Whoever therefore relaxes one of the least of these commandments and so teaches others, shall be called least in the kingdom of the heavens; but whoever does and teaches them, this one shall be called great in the kingdom of the heavens.
But when Herod was dead, behold, an angel of the Lord appeareth in a dream to Joseph in Egypt, saying,
ὃς ἐὰν οὖν λύσῃ μίαν τῶν ἐντολῶν τούτων τῶν ἐλαχίστων καὶ διδάξῃ οὕτως τοὺς ἀνθρώπους, ἐλάχιστος κληθήσεται ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν· ὃς δ' ἂν ποιήσῃ καὶ διδάξῃ, οὗτος μέγας κληθήσεται ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν.
Translation Commentary Verse 19

The escalation-clause: those who break-and-teach-others-to-break the commandments will be elachistos (least) in the kingdom; those who do-and-teach-them will be megas (great). The Matthean Jesus reinforces Torah-observance at the highest pitch.

20
For I say to you that unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you shall not enter the kingdom of the heavens.
Arise and take the young child and his mother, and go into the land of Israel: for they are dead that sought the young child`s life.
λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐὰν μὴ περισσεύσῃ ὑμῶν ἡ δικαιοσύνη πλεῖον τῶν γραμματέων καὶ Φαρισαίων, οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθητε εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν.
Translation Commentary Verse 20

ean mē perisseusē hymōn hē dikaiosynē pleion tōn grammateōn kai Pharisaiōn — 'unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees'. The Matthean intensification: the SM-ethic exceeds Pharisaic Torah-observance, not replaces it. The polemical-edge against scribes-and-Pharisees is a Matthean redactional feature; modern Jewish-Christian dialogue (Levine 2006; JANT 2017) emphasizes that the 1st-c. polemic is intra-Jewish, not anti-Jewish, and supersessionist readings are downstream Christian-misappropriations.

21
You have heard that it was said to those of old: "You shall not murder"; and whoever murders shall be liable to judgment.
And he arose and took the young child and his mother, and came into the land of Israel.
Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη τοῖς ἀρχαίοις· Οὐ φονεύσεις· ὃς δ' ἂν φονεύσῃ, ἔνοχος ἔσται τῇ κρίσει.
Translation Commentary Verse 21

The first antithesis (vv.21-26) on murder/anger. errethē tois archaiois ... egō de legō hymin — the antithetical-formula 'you have heard it said ... but I say to you' opens the six antitheses. The formula does NOT abrogate Torah; it intensifies-and-internalizes (anger as root of murder; lust as root of adultery). Davies-Allison ICC 1.504-510.

22
But I say to you that everyone who is angry with his brother shall be liable to judgment; and whoever says to his brother, "Raca" (empty-head), shall be liable to the council; and whoever says, "You fool," shall be liable to the gehenna of fire.
But when he heard that Archelaus was reigning over Judaea in the room of his father Herod, he was afraid to go thither; and being warned [of God] in a dream, he withdrew into the parts of Galilee,
ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ὀργιζόμενος τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ ἔνοχος ἔσται τῇ κρίσει· ὃς δ' ἂν εἴπῃ τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ· Ῥακά, ἔνοχος ἔσται τῷ συνεδρίῳ· ὃς δ' ἂν εἴπῃ· Μωρέ, ἔνοχος ἔσται εἰς τὴν γέενναν τοῦ πυρός.
Translation Commentary Verse 22

rhaka — Greek transliteration of Aramaic reqaʾ 'empty-headed one, fool'. Matthew preserves the Aramaic loan-word untranslated, evidencing the Aramaic-substratum of the Jesus-tradition. Three-fold judgment escalation: anger → judgment; rhaka → council; mōre → gehenna-of-fire. See overlay entry raca-aramaic-insult-untranslated-mt-5-22.

23
If therefore you are bringing your gift to the altar and there remember that your brother has something against you,
and came and dwelt in a city called Nazareth; that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through the prophets, that he should be called a Nazarene.
ἐὰν οὖν προσφέρῃς τὸ δῶρόν σου ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον κἀκεῖ μνησθῇς ὅτι ὁ ἀδελφός σου ἔχει τι κατὰ σοῦ,
24
leave your gift there before the altar and go: first be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift.
ἄφες ἐκεῖ τὸ δῶρόν σου ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου καὶ ὕπαγε πρῶτον διαλλάγηθι τῷ ἀδελφῷ σου, καὶ τότε ἐλθὼν πρόσφερε τὸ δῶρόν σου.
25
Make friends quickly with your accuser while you are with him on the way, lest your accuser hand you over to the judge, and the judge to the officer, and you be thrown into prison.
ἴσθι εὐνοῶν τῷ ἀντιδίκῳ σου ταχὺ ἕως ὅτου εἶ μετ' αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ, μήποτέ σε παραδῷ ὁ ἀντίδικος τῷ κριτῇ, καὶ ὁ κριτὴς τῷ ὑπηρέτῃ, καὶ εἰς φυλακὴν βληθήσῃ·
26
Amen I say to you, you shall by no means come out from there until you have paid the last quadrans.
ἀμὴν λέγω σοι, οὐ μὴ ἐξέλθῃς ἐκεῖθεν ἕως ἂν ἀποδῷς τὸν ἔσχατον κοδράντην.
27
You have heard that it was said: "You shall not commit adultery."
Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη· Οὐ μοιχεύσεις.
Translation Commentary Verse 27

The second antithesis (vv.27-30) on adultery/lust. The intensification: not only the act but the look-with-intent (epithymēsai autēn) constitutes adultery. The Matthean ethics internalizes Torah at the level of intention. Davies-Allison ICC 1.521-525.

28
But I say to you that everyone who looks at a woman to desire her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ βλέπων γυναῖκα πρὸς τὸ ἐπιθυμῆσαι αὐτὴν ἤδη ἐμοίχευσεν αὐτὴν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ.
29
If your right eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it from you; for it is better for you that one of your members perish, than that your whole body be thrown into gehenna.
εἰ δὲ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ὁ δεξιὸς σκανδαλίζει σε, ἔξελε αὐτὸν καὶ βάλε ἀπὸ σοῦ, συμφέρει γάρ σοι ἵνα ἀπόληται ἓν τῶν μελῶν σου καὶ μὴ ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου βληθῇ εἰς γέενναν.
30
And if your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it from you; for it is better for you that one of your members perish, than that your whole body go away into gehenna.
καὶ εἰ ἡ δεξιά σου χεὶρ σκανδαλίζει σε, ἔκκοψον αὐτὴν καὶ βάλε ἀπὸ σοῦ, συμφέρει γάρ σοι ἵνα ἀπόληται ἓν τῶν μελῶν σου καὶ μὴ ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου εἰς γέενναν ἀπέλθῃ.
31
It was also said: "Whoever divorces his wife, let him give her a certificate of divorce."
Ἐρρέθη δέ· Ὃς ἂν ἀπολύσῃ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ, δότω αὐτῇ ἀποστάσιον.
Translation Commentary Verse 31

The third antithesis (vv.31-32) on divorce. apolyō + apostasion — the bill-of-divorcement (Deut 24:1). The Matthean exception-clause parektos logou porneias ('except for sexual-immorality') is a Matthean addition not in Mk 10:11 or Lk 16:18. The exception-clause is one of the most-debated Matthean Torah-redactions in the history of Christian moral-theology. Davies-Allison ICC 1.527-532.

32
But I say to you that everyone who divorces his wife, except on the ground of unchastity, causes her to commit adultery, and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ἀπολύων τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ παρεκτὸς λόγου πορνείας ποιεῖ αὐτὴν μοιχευθῆναι, καὶ ὃς ἐὰν ἀπολελυμένην γαμήσῃ μοιχᾶται.
33
Again, you have heard that it was said to those of old: "You shall not swear falsely, but shall perform to the Lord what you have sworn."
Πάλιν ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη τοῖς ἀρχαίοις· Οὐκ ἐπιορκήσεις, ἀποδώσεις δὲ τῷ κυρίῳ τοὺς ὅρκους σου.
Translation Commentary Verse 33

The fourth antithesis (vv.33-37) on oaths. The Matthean Jesus' radical prohibition (mē omosai holōs 'do not swear at all') goes beyond Torah's regulation-of-oaths. Cross-corpus to Jas 5:12; Philo Decal. 84-95 (Hellenistic-Jewish oath-criticism); Qumran-community oath-prohibition (4Q477).

34
But I say to you, do not swear at all: neither by heaven, for it is the throne of God,
ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν μὴ ὀμόσαι ὅλως· μήτε ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, ὅτι θρόνος ἐστὶν τοῦ θεοῦ·
35
nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of his feet; nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King;
μήτε ἐν τῇ γῇ, ὅτι ὑποπόδιόν ἐστιν τῶν ποδῶν αὐτοῦ· μήτε εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, ὅτι πόλις ἐστὶν τοῦ μεγάλου βασιλέως·
36
nor shall you swear by your head, for you cannot make one hair white or black.
μήτε ἐν τῇ κεφαλῇ σου ὀμόσῃς, ὅτι οὐ δύνασαι μίαν τρίχα λευκὴν ποιῆσαι ἢ μέλαιναν.
37
But let your word be "Yes, yes," "No, no"; anything beyond these is from the evil one.
ἔστω δὲ ὁ λόγος ὑμῶν ναὶ ναί, οὒ οὔ· τὸ δὲ περισσὸν τούτων ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ ἐστιν.
38
You have heard that it was said: "An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth."
Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη· Ὀφθαλμὸν ἀντὶ ὀφθαλμοῦ καὶ ὀδόντα ἀντὶ ὀδόντος.
Translation Commentary Verse 38

The fifth antithesis (vv.38-42) on retaliation. Ophthalmon anti ophthalmou — the lex talionis (Ex 21:24; Lev 24:20; Deut 19:21). The Matthean Jesus' non-retaliation teaching does not abrogate Torah's judicial-principle but transforms-it for inter-personal ethics. Davies-Allison ICC 1.540-548.

39
But I say to you, do not resist the evildoer; but whoever strikes you on the right cheek, turn to him the other also.
ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν μὴ ἀντιστῆναι τῷ πονηρῷ· ἀλλ' ὅστις σε ῥαπίζει εἰς τὴν δεξιὰν σιαγόνα, στρέψον αὐτῷ καὶ τὴν ἄλλην·
40
And to the one who wishes to sue you and take your tunic, hand over your cloak also.
καὶ τῷ θέλοντί σοι κριθῆναι καὶ τὸν χιτῶνά σου λαβεῖν, ἄφες αὐτῷ καὶ τὸ ἱμάτιον·
41
And whoever compels you to go one mile, go with him two.
καὶ ὅστις σε ἀγγαρεύσει μίλιον ἕν, ὕπαγε μετ' αὐτοῦ δύο.
42
Give to the one who asks of you, and do not turn away from the one who wishes to borrow from you.
τῷ αἰτοῦντί σε δός, καὶ τὸν θέλοντα ἀπὸ σοῦ δανίσασθαι μὴ ἀποστραφῇς.
43
You have heard that it was said: "You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy."
Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη· Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου καὶ μισήσεις τὸν ἐχθρόν σου.
Translation Commentary Verse 43

The sixth antithesis (vv.43-48) on enemy-love. agapēseis ton plēsion sou — Lev 19:18 LXX. The miseseis ton echthron sou 'you shall hate your enemy' is NOT a Torah citation; it appears at Qumran (1QS 1:10 li-snoʾ kol benei ḥošek 'to hate all the sons of darkness'), suggesting the Matthean Jesus engages a Qumran-sectarian rather than mainstream-rabbinic position. Davies-Allison ICC 1.549-553.

44
But I say to you, love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,
ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑμῶν καὶ προσεύχεσθε ὑπὲρ τῶν διωκόντων ὑμᾶς·
45
so that you may be sons of your Father who is in the heavens, for he makes his sun rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous.
ὅπως γένησθε υἱοὶ τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς, ὅτι τὸν ἥλιον αὐτοῦ ἀνατέλλει ἐπὶ πονηροὺς καὶ ἀγαθοὺς καὶ βρέχει ἐπὶ δικαίους καὶ ἀδίκους.
46
For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the same?
ἐὰν γὰρ ἀγαπήσητε τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας ὑμᾶς, τίνα μισθὸν ἔχετε; οὐχὶ καὶ οἱ τελῶναι τὸ αὐτὸ ποιοῦσιν;
47
And if you greet only your brothers, what more are you doing? Do not even the Gentiles do the same?
καὶ ἐὰν ἀσπάσησθε τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ὑμῶν μόνον, τί περισσὸν ποιεῖτε; οὐχὶ καὶ οἱ ἐθνικοὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ποιοῦσιν;
48
You therefore shall be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.
Ἔσεσθε οὖν ὑμεῖς τέλειοι ὡς ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος τέλειός ἐστιν.
Translation Commentary Verse 48

esesthe oun hymeis teleioi hōs ho patēr hymōn ho ouranios teleios estin — 'be perfect as your heavenly Father is perfect'. The Matthean teleios echoes Lev 19:2 qĕdōšîm tihyû kī qādôš ʾanî YHWH ʾĕlōhêkem 'be holy for I YHWH your God am holy' (the Holiness Code parallel) — teleios in NT-Greek functionally renders Hebrew tāmîm 'whole, blameless, complete'. The closing-statement of the antitheses-section frames the entire SM-ethic as a holiness-imitation. Davies-Allison ICC 1.560-563.

Chapter 6

Matthew 6 — Sermon on the Mount Pt II: alms, the Lord's Prayer, fasting, treasure in heaven, anxiety

1
Take care not to practice your righteousness before people in order to be seen by them; for if you do, you have no reward from your Father who is in the heavens.
And in those days cometh John the Baptist, preaching in the wilderness of Judaea, saying,
Προσέχετε δὲ τὴν δικαιοσύνην ὑμῶν μὴ ποιεῖν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων πρὸς τὸ θεαθῆναι αὐτοῖς· εἰ δὲ μή γε, μισθὸν οὐκ ἔχετε παρὰ τῷ πατρὶ ὑμῶν τῷ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.
Translation Commentary Verse 1

prosechete tēn dikaiosynēn hymōn mē poiein emprosthen tōn anthrōpōn — 'beware of practicing your righteousness before others'. The Matthean redactional-hinge introducing the three-fold piety-section (alms / prayer / fasting) where each piety-practice is treated against the hypokrisis (public-display) anti-pattern. The Matthean Jesus' critique targets ostentatious-piety, not the practices themselves.

2
So when you give alms, do not sound a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may be praised by people. Amen I say to you, they have received their reward.
Repent ye; for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
Ὅταν οὖν ποιῇς ἐλεημοσύνην, μὴ σαλπίσῃς ἔμπροσθέν σου, ὥσπερ οἱ ὑποκριταὶ ποιοῦσιν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ ἐν ταῖς ῥύμαις, ὅπως δοξασθῶσιν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν.
Translation Commentary Verse 2

hypokritai — 'hypocrites', literally 'actors' (one playing-a-role on stage). The Matthean technical term for the public-display anti-pattern. The critique is intra-Jewish (the Matthean community is Jewish-Christian) and addresses the temptation to ostentatious-piety; the supersessionist generalization 'Jews are hypocrites' is a downstream Christian-anti-Judaic misreading. Davies-Allison ICC 1.578-580.

3
But when you give alms, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,
For this is he that was spoken of through Isaiah the prophet, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make ye ready the way of the Lord, Make his paths straight.
σοῦ δὲ ποιοῦντος ἐλεημοσύνην μὴ γνώτω ἡ ἀριστερά σου τί ποιεῖ ἡ δεξιά σου,
4
so that your alms may be in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.
Now John himself had his raiment of camel`s hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins; and his food was locusts and wild honey.
ὅπως ᾖ σου ἡ ἐλεημοσύνη ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ· καὶ ὁ πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ ἀποδώσει σοι.
5
And when you pray, you shall not be like the hypocrites, for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and at the street corners, that they may be seen by people. Amen I say to you, they have received their reward.
Then went out unto him Jerusalem, and all Judaea, and all the region round about the Jordan;
Καὶ ὅταν προσεύχησθε, οὐκ ἔσεσθε ὡς οἱ ὑποκριταί· ὅτι φιλοῦσιν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ ἐν ταῖς γωνίαις τῶν πλατειῶν ἑστῶτες προσεύχεσθαι, ὅπως φανῶσιν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν.
Translation Commentary Verse 5

hotan proseuchēsthe ... ouk esesthe hōs hoi hypokritai — the prayer-section opens with the same hypokritai warning against public-display. Cross-corpus to the Qumran Hodayot communal-prayer tradition; the Pharisaic-rabbinic tradition itself develops critiques of ostentatious-piety (m.Sotah 3:4 the seven-types-of-Pharisees).

6
But you, when you pray, go into your inner room, and shutting your door, pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.
and they were baptized of him in the river Jordan, confessing their sins.
σὺ δὲ ὅταν προσεύχῃ, εἴσελθε εἰς τὸ ταμεῖόν σου καὶ κλείσας τὴν θύραν σου πρόσευξαι τῷ πατρί σου τῷ ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ· καὶ ὁ πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ ἀποδώσει σοι.
7
And in praying, do not babble as the Gentiles do, for they think they will be heard for their many words.
But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his baptism, he said unto them, Ye offspring of vipers, who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?
Προσευχόμενοι δὲ μὴ βατταλογήσητε ὥσπερ οἱ ἐθνικοί, δοκοῦσιν γὰρ ὅτι ἐν τῇ πολυλογίᾳ αὐτῶν εἰσακουσθήσονται.
8
Therefore do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask him.
Bring forth therefore fruit worthy of repentance:
μὴ οὖν ὁμοιωθῆτε αὐτοῖς, οἶδεν γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὧν χρείαν ἔχετε πρὸ τοῦ ὑμᾶς αἰτῆσαι αὐτόν.
9
Pray then in this way: Our Father who are in the heavens, hallowed be your name,
and think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.
Οὕτως οὖν προσεύχεσθε ὑμεῖς· Πάτερ ἡμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς, ἁγιασθήτω τὸ ὄνομά σου,
Translation Commentary Verse 9

The Lord's Prayer opens. Pater hēmōn ho en tois ouranois — 'our Father in the heavens'. Cross-corpus to the Jewish liturgical-tradition: Avinu she-ba-shamayim (Our Father in heaven), the Kaddish opening yitgadal we-yitkadash shemeh rabba (may his great name be magnified and sanctified). hagiasthētō to onoma sou directly echoes the Kaddish sanctification. The Matthean Lord's Prayer is rooted in Jewish liturgical-prayer structures. See lords-prayer-mt-6-9-13-pater-hēmōn-byzantine-doxology-textual-variant-cross-corpus.

10
your kingdom come, your will be done, as in heaven, so also on earth.
And even now the axe lieth at the root of the trees: every tree therefore that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire.
ἐλθέτω ἡ βασιλεία σου, γενηθήτω τὸ θέλημά σου, ὡς ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς.
Translation Commentary Verse 10

eltheto hē basileia sou; genēthētō to thelēma sou — 'your kingdom come; your will be done'. Echoes the Kaddish's we-yamlikh malkhuteh ('and may he establish his kingship'); echoes 1 Macc 3:60 hōs an ē thelēma en ouranō, houtōs poiēsei ('as may be the will in heaven, so shall he do'). See kingdom-of-heaven-basileia-tōn-ouranōn-mt-distinctive-cross-corpus-hebrew-malkhut-shamayim.

11
Give us this day our daily bread;
I indeed baptize you in water unto repentance: but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you in the Holy Spirit and [in] fire:
Τὸν ἄρτον ἡμῶν τὸν ἐπιούσιον δὸς ἡμῖν σήμερον·
Translation Commentary Verse 11

ton arton hēmōn ton epiousion — the epiousios hapax legomenon (unattested in pre-NT Greek). Three competing renderings: 'daily' (the dominant English-tradition); 'for-tomorrow' (Jerome's Lk 11:3 'crastinum'; Jeremias 1971 reconstruction from Aramaic yoma de-yatya); 'supersubstantial' (Jerome's Mt 6:11 'supersubstantialem'; the Catholic Eucharistic-reading). The WoH-Translation preserves 'daily' per the dominant convention; see overlay entry epiousios-hapax-translation-convention.

12
and forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors;
whose fan is in his hand, and he will thoroughly cleanse his threshing-floor; and he will gather his wheat into the garner, but the chaff he will burn up with unquenchable fire.
καὶ ἄφες ἡμῖν τὰ ὀφειλήματα ἡμῶν, ὡς καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀφήκαμεν τοῖς ὀφειλέταις ἡμῶν·
Translation Commentary Verse 12

ta opheilēmata hēmōn — 'our debts' (literal-financial-debt metaphor for sin). The Matthean choice of opheilēmata (vs Lukan hamartias 'sins' at Lk 11:4) preserves the Aramaic ḥobaʾ (debt-as-sin metaphor) more directly. The forgive-as-we-forgive conditional is a distinctive Matthean theological-feature reinforced at Mt 6:14-15 and Mt 18:23-35 (the unforgiving-servant parable).

13
and do not bring us into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.
Then cometh Jesus from Galilee to the Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him.
καὶ μὴ εἰσενέγκῃς ἡμᾶς εἰς πειρασμόν, ἀλλὰ ῥῦσαι ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ πονηροῦ.
Translation Commentary Verse 13

mē eisenenkēs hēmas eis peirasmon, alla rhysai hēmas apo tou ponērou — 'do not lead us into testing, but deliver us from the evil one'. peirasmos covers both 'testing/trial' (eschatological-testing) and 'temptation' (moral-seduction); the eschatological-testing sense is the more-likely Matthean horizon. tou ponērou admits masculine 'the evil one' (Satan) or neuter 'evil' generically; the masculine reading is supported by Mt 13:19, 13:38. Textual variant: the Byzantine doxology hoti sou estin hē basileia kai hē dynamis kai hē doxa eis tous aiōnas, amēn is absent in B + א + critical text. See overlay entry lords-prayer-doxology-textual-variant-convention.

14
For if you forgive others their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you;
But John would have hindered him, saying, I have need to be baptized of thee, and comest thou to me?
ἐὰν γὰρ ἀφῆτε τοῖς ἀνθρώποις τὰ παραπτώματα αὐτῶν, ἀφήσει καὶ ὑμῖν ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος·
15
but if you do not forgive others, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.
But Jesus answering said unto him, Suffer [it] now: for thus it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness. Then he suffereth him.
ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ἀφῆτε τοῖς ἀνθρώποις, οὐδὲ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ἀφήσει τὰ παραπτώματα ὑμῶν.
16
And when you fast, do not be gloomy-faced like the hypocrites; for they disfigure their faces, that they may be seen by people to be fasting. Amen I say to you, they have received their reward.
And Jesus when he was baptized, went up straightway from the water: and lo, the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Spirit of God descending as a dove, and coming upon him;
Ὅταν δὲ νηστεύητε, μὴ γίνεσθε ὡς οἱ ὑποκριταὶ σκυθρωποί, ἀφανίζουσιν γὰρ τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν ὅπως φανῶσιν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις νηστεύοντες· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν.
Translation Commentary Verse 16

hotan de nēsteuēte ... hōs hoi hypokritai — the fasting-section, closing the three-fold piety-pattern. Cross-corpus to Isa 58:1-9 (the prophetic critique of ostentatious-fasting and the call for justice-as-true-fasting). Davies-Allison ICC 1.616-620.

17
But you, when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face,
and lo, a voice out of the heavens, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.
σὺ δὲ νηστεύων ἄλειψαί σου τὴν κεφαλὴν καὶ τὸ πρόσωπόν σου νίψαι,
18
so that you may not be seen by people to be fasting, but by your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.
ὅπως μὴ φανῇς τοῖς ἀνθρώποις νηστεύων ἀλλὰ τῷ πατρί σου τῷ ἐν τῷ κρυφαίῳ· καὶ ὁ πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυφαίῳ ἀποδώσει σοι.
19
Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust consume, and where thieves break in and steal;
Μὴ θησαυρίζετε ὑμῖν θησαυροὺς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ὅπου σὴς καὶ βρῶσις ἀφανίζει, καὶ ὅπου κλέπται διορύσσουσιν καὶ κλέπτουσιν·
Translation Commentary Verse 19

mē thēsaurizete hymin thēsaurous epi tēs gēs — 'do not store up treasures on earth'. The treasure-in-heaven teaching has cross-corpus parallels: Sir 29:11 'lay up your treasure according to the commandments of the Most High'; Tob 4:8-9 (Tobit's almsgiving-treasure-in-heaven counsel); 4 Ezra 6:5; 7:77 (the apocalyptic-treasury-of-merit tradition). The Matthean teaching is rooted in Jewish-wisdom tradition.

20
but store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust consumes, and where thieves do not break in or steal.
θησαυρίζετε δὲ ὑμῖν θησαυροὺς ἐν οὐρανῷ, ὅπου οὔτε σὴς οὔτε βρῶσις ἀφανίζει, καὶ ὅπου κλέπται οὐ διορύσσουσιν οὐδὲ κλέπτουσιν·
21
For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
ὅπου γάρ ἐστιν ὁ θησαυρός σου, ἐκεῖ ἔσται καὶ ἡ καρδία σου.
22
The lamp of the body is the eye. If therefore your eye is sound, your whole body will be full of light;
Ὁ λύχνος τοῦ σώματός ἐστιν ὁ ὀφθαλμός. ἐὰν οὖν ᾖ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ἁπλοῦς, ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου φωτεινὸν ἔσται·
Translation Commentary Verse 22

ho lychnos tou sōmatos estin ho ophthalmos — the eye-as-lamp-of-the-body saying. The ophthalmos haplous (single/healthy eye) vs ponēros (evil/bad eye) is rooted in Jewish-tradition: a haplous/single eye marks generosity (Sir 32:8; T. Iss. 3:4); an ophthalmos ponēros/evil eye marks envy/stinginess (Deut 15:9 ʿênĕkā ḥātĕṭâ ʾāḥîkā 'your eye is begrudging toward your brother'; Prov 23:6; 28:22).

23
but if your eye is evil, your whole body will be full of darkness. If then the light that is in you is darkness, how great is the darkness!
ἐὰν δὲ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου πονηρὸς ᾖ, ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου σκοτεινὸν ἔσται. εἰ οὖν τὸ φῶς τὸ ἐν σοὶ σκότος ἐστίν, τὸ σκότος πόσον.
24
No one is able to serve two masters; for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and mammon.
Οὐδεὶς δύναται δυσὶ κυρίοις δουλεύειν· ἢ γὰρ τὸν ἕνα μισήσει καὶ τὸν ἕτερον ἀγαπήσει, ἢ ἑνὸς ἀνθέξεται καὶ τοῦ ἑτέρου καταφρονήσει. οὐ δύνασθε θεῷ δουλεύειν καὶ μαμωνᾷ.
Translation Commentary Verse 24

oudeis dynatai dysi kyriois douleuein ... ou dynasthe theō douleuein kai mamōna — 'you cannot serve God and mammon'. mamōnas is an Aramaic loan-word (māmôn 'wealth, property'), preserved untranslated by Matthew. The Aramaic-loan-preservation parallel to rhaka at 5:22, amēn throughout, kephas in Pauline tradition.

25
Therefore I say to you, do not be anxious about your life, what you shall eat or what you shall drink; nor about your body, what you shall put on. Is not the life more than food, and the body more than clothing?
Διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν· μὴ μεριμνᾶτε τῇ ψυχῇ ὑμῶν τί φάγητε ἢ τί πίητε, μηδὲ τῷ σώματι ὑμῶν τί ἐνδύσησθε· οὐχὶ ἡ ψυχὴ πλεῖόν ἐστιν τῆς τροφῆς καὶ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ ἐνδύματος;
Translation Commentary Verse 25

mē merimnate tē psychē hymōn — 'do not be anxious for your life'. The anxiety-section (vv.25-34) is rooted in Jewish-wisdom (Sir 30:21-25; Sir 38:18-19 on care-and-anxiety; Ps 55:22; Prov 12:25) and addresses peasant-Galilean economic-anxiety in concrete terms. Davies-Allison ICC 1.647-656.

26
Look at the birds of the sky: they do not sow, nor reap, nor gather into barns; and your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not of more value than they?
ἐμβλέψατε εἰς τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ὅτι οὐ σπείρουσιν οὐδὲ θερίζουσιν οὐδὲ συνάγουσιν εἰς ἀποθήκας, καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος τρέφει αὐτά· οὐχ ὑμεῖς μᾶλλον διαφέρετε αὐτῶν;
27
And which of you by being anxious is able to add one cubit to his span of life?
τίς δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν μεριμνῶν δύναται προσθεῖναι ἐπὶ τὴν ἡλικίαν αὐτοῦ πῆχυν ἕνα;
28
And why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow: they do not toil nor spin;
καὶ περὶ ἐνδύματος τί μεριμνᾶτε; καταμάθετε τὰ κρίνα τοῦ ἀγροῦ πῶς αὐξάνουσιν· οὐ κοπιῶσιν οὐδὲ νήθουσιν·
29
yet I say to you, not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.
λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδὲ Σολομὼν ἐν πάσῃ τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ περιεβάλετο ὡς ἓν τούτων.
30
But if God so clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, will he not much more clothe you, O you of little faith?
εἰ δὲ τὸν χόρτον τοῦ ἀγροῦ σήμερον ὄντα καὶ αὔριον εἰς κλίβανον βαλλόμενον ὁ θεὸς οὕτως ἀμφιέννυσιν, οὐ πολλῷ μᾶλλον ὑμᾶς, ὀλιγόπιστοι;
31
Therefore do not be anxious, saying, "What shall we eat?" or "What shall we drink?" or "What shall we wear?"
μὴ οὖν μεριμνήσητε λέγοντες· Τί φάγωμεν; ἤ· Τί πίωμεν; ἤ· Τί περιβαλώμεθα;
32
For the Gentiles seek after all these things; and your heavenly Father knows that you need them all.
πάντα γὰρ ταῦτα τὰ ἔθνη ἐπιζητοῦσιν· οἶδεν γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος ὅτι χρῄζετε τούτων ἁπάντων.
33
But seek first the kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things shall be added to you.
ζητεῖτε δὲ πρῶτον τὴν βασιλείαν καὶ τὴν δικαιοσύνην αὐτοῦ, καὶ ταῦτα πάντα προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν.
Translation Commentary Verse 33

zēteite de prōton tēn basileian kai tēn dikaiosynēn autou — 'seek first the kingdom and his righteousness'. The Matthean basileia + dikaiosynē pairing closes the anxiety-discourse with the central Matthean theological-pair: the kingdom-of-the-heavens (the eschatological reign) + righteousness (the SM-ethical-program).

34
Therefore do not be anxious about tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Sufficient for the day is its own trouble.
μὴ οὖν μεριμνήσητε εἰς τὴν αὔριον, ἡ γὰρ αὔριον μεριμνήσει ἑαυτῆς· ἀρκετὸν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἡ κακία αὐτῆς.
Translation Commentary Verse 34

arketon tē hēmera hē kakia autēs — 'sufficient for the day is its own evil'. Closing-aphorism; rooted in Jewish-wisdom (cf. Sir 11:23-24).

Chapter 7

Matthew 7 — Sermon on the Mount Pt III: judgment, ask-seek-knock, the golden rule, the narrow gate, the two builders

1
Do not judge, so that you may not be judged.
Then was Jesus led up of the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil.
Μὴ κρίνετε, ἵνα μὴ κριθῆτε·
Translation Commentary Verse 1

mē krinete hina mē krithēte — 'do not judge, lest you be judged'. The judgment-section opens with a wisdom-tradition reciprocity-principle (cf. m.Sotah 1:7 'with whatever measure a person measures, it shall be measured to him'). The Matthean teaching critiques harsh-judgment-of-others within the community, not all-judgment-as-such. Davies-Allison ICC 1.668-672.

2
For with the judgment you pronounce you will be judged, and with the measure you use it will be measured to you.
And when he had fasted forty days and forty nights, he afterward hungered.
ἐν ᾧ γὰρ κρίματι κρίνετε κριθήσεσθε, καὶ ἐν ᾧ μέτρῳ μετρεῖτε μετρηθήσεται ὑμῖν.
3
Why do you see the speck that is in your brother's eye, but do not notice the beam that is in your own eye?
And the tempter came and said unto him, If thou art the Son of God, command that these stones become bread.
τί δὲ βλέπεις τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου, τὴν δὲ ἐν τῷ σῷ ὀφθαλμῷ δοκὸν οὐ κατανοεῖς;
Translation Commentary Verse 3

ti de blepeis to karphos to en tō ophthalmō tou adelphou sou — the speck-and-plank hyperbole. Rabbinic-parallel: b.Arak. 16b 'remove the splinter from between your teeth, and they will say, remove the beam from between your eyes'. The hyperbolic rhetorical-style is characteristic of Jewish-wisdom and the Matthean Jesus-tradition.

4
Or how can you say to your brother, "Let me take the speck out of your eye," while behold, the beam is in your own eye?
But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.
ἢ πῶς ἐρεῖς τῷ ἀδελφῷ σου· Ἄφες ἐκβάλω τὸ κάρφος ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ σου, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἡ δοκὸς ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ σοῦ;
5
You hypocrite, first take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your brother's eye.
Then the devil taketh him into the holy city; and he set him on the pinnacle of the temple,
ὑποκριτά, ἔκβαλε πρῶτον ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ σοῦ τὴν δοκόν, καὶ τότε διαβλέψεις ἐκβαλεῖν τὸ κάρφος ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου.
6
Do not give what is holy to dogs, nor cast your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and turn and tear you to pieces.
and saith unto him, If thou art the Son of God, cast thyself down: for it is written, He shall give his angels charge concerning thee: and, On their hands they shall bear thee up, Lest haply thou dash thy foot against a stone.
Μὴ δῶτε τὸ ἅγιον τοῖς κυσίν, μηδὲ βάλητε τοὺς μαργαρίτας ὑμῶν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν χοίρων, μήποτε καταπατήσουσιν αὐτοὺς ἐν τοῖς ποσὶν αὐτῶν καὶ στραφέντες ῥήξωσιν ὑμᾶς.
Translation Commentary Verse 6

mē dōte to hagion tois kysin mēde balēte tous margaritas hymōn emprosthen tōn choirōn — 'do not give what is holy to the dogs ... pearls before swine'. Aphoristic-wisdom protecting sacred-teaching from desecration. The verse has been deployed in early-Christian Eucharistic discipline (Didache 9:5); the original Matthean horizon is broader-than-Eucharistic. Davies-Allison ICC 1.674-678.

7
Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
Jesus said unto him, Again it is written, Thou shalt not make trial of the Lord thy God.
Αἰτεῖτε, καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν· ζητεῖτε, καὶ εὑρήσετε· κρούετε, καὶ ἀνοιγήσεται ὑμῖν.
Translation Commentary Verse 7

aiteite ... zēteite ... krouete — the three-fold ask-seek-knock aphorism. Generally treated as a Q-source saying preserved in both Matthew and Lk 11:9-13. The Matthean patēr hymōn ho en ouranois (v.11) closes the section with the Matthean-distinctive Father-in-the-heavens-formula echoing the Lord's Prayer (6:9).

8
For everyone who asks receives, and the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened.
Again, the devil taketh him unto an exceeding high mountain, and showeth him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them;
πᾶς γὰρ ὁ αἰτῶν λαμβάνει καὶ ὁ ζητῶν εὑρίσκει καὶ τῷ κρούοντι ἀνοιγήσεται.
9
Or what man is there among you, whose son will ask him for bread — will he give him a stone?
and he said unto him, All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me.
ἢ τίς ἐστιν ἐξ ὑμῶν ἄνθρωπος, ὃν αἰτήσει ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ ἄρτον — μὴ λίθον ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ;
10
Or if he asks for a fish, will he give him a snake?
Then saith Jesus unto him, Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.
ἢ καὶ ἰχθὺν αἰτήσει — μὴ ὄφιν ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ;
11
If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father who is in the heavens give good things to those who ask him.
Then the devil leaveth him; and behold, angels came and ministered unto him.
εἰ οὖν ὑμεῖς πονηροὶ ὄντες οἴδατε δόματα ἀγαθὰ διδόναι τοῖς τέκνοις ὑμῶν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς δώσει ἀγαθὰ τοῖς αἰτοῦσιν αὐτόν.
12
Therefore everything that you wish people to do for you, so also do you to them; for this is the Law and the Prophets.
Now when he heard that John was delivered up, he withdrew into Galilee;
Πάντα οὖν ὅσα ἐὰν θέλητε ἵνα ποιῶσιν ὑμῖν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ποιεῖτε αὐτοῖς· οὗτος γάρ ἐστιν ὁ νόμος καὶ οἱ προφῆται.
Translation Commentary Verse 12

The Golden Rule. Panta oun hosa ean thelēte hina poiōsin hymin hoi anthrōpoi, houtōs kai hymeis poieite autois — positive-formulation. Cross-corpus parallel to Hillel's b.Shabbat 31a negative-formulation 'what is hateful to you, do not do to your fellow' (the Hillel-rule explicitly identified as 'the whole Torah'); Tobit 4:15 (negative-formulation, 3rd-2nd c. BCE); Confucius Analects 15.23 (negative-formulation, 6th-5th c. BCE); Letter of Aristeas 207. The Matthean closing houtos gar estin ho nomos kai hoi prophētai explicitly identifies the rule as a Torah-summary, structurally paralleling Mt 22:40 and forming inclusio with Mt 5:17. See golden-rule-mt-7-12-hillel-cross-corpus.

13
Enter through the narrow gate; for wide is the gate and broad the way that leads to destruction, and many are those who enter through it.
and leaving Nazareth, he came and dwelt in Capernaum, which is by the sea, in the borders of Zebulun and Naphtali:
Εἰσέλθατε διὰ τῆς στενῆς πύλης· ὅτι πλατεῖα ἡ πύλη καὶ εὐρύχωρος ἡ ὁδὸς ἡ ἀπάγουσα εἰς τὴν ἀπώλειαν, καὶ πολλοί εἰσιν οἱ εἰσερχόμενοι δι' αὐτῆς·
Translation Commentary Verse 13

eiselthate dia tēs stenēs pylēs — 'enter through the narrow gate'. The two-ways tradition is rooted in Jewish-wisdom (Deut 30:15-20 the life-and-death paths; Ps 1 the two-ways psalm; Jer 21:8 'I set before you the way of life and the way of death'; Sir 21:10; Did. 1:1 'two ways, one of life and one of death'). Davies-Allison ICC 1.694-698.

14
How narrow is the gate and constricted the way that leads to life, and few are those who find it!
that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying,
τί στενὴ ἡ πύλη καὶ τεθλιμμένη ἡ ὁδὸς ἡ ἀπάγουσα εἰς τὴν ζωήν, καὶ ὀλίγοι εἰσὶν οἱ εὑρίσκοντες αὐτήν.
15
Beware of the false prophets, who come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly are ravenous wolves.
The land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, Toward the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles,
Προσέχετε ἀπὸ τῶν ψευδοπροφητῶν, οἵτινες ἔρχονται πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐν ἐνδύμασι προβάτων, ἔσωθεν δέ εἰσιν λύκοι ἅρπαγες.
Translation Commentary Verse 15

prosechete apo tōn pseudoprophētōn — 'beware of false prophets'. The false-prophets warning continues the eschatological-test-of-discernment tradition (Deut 13:2-6; Jer 23:9-40; Ezek 13). The Matthean horizon addresses both external-false-prophets and intra-community false-teachers (Mt 24:11, 24).

16
By their fruits you will recognize them. Do they gather grapes from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?
The people that sat in darkness Saw a great light, And to them that sat in the region and shadow of death, To them did light spring up.
ἀπὸ τῶν καρπῶν αὐτῶν ἐπιγνώσεσθε αὐτούς· μήτι συλλέγουσιν ἀπὸ ἀκανθῶν σταφυλὰς ἢ ἀπὸ τριβόλων σῦκα;
17
So every good tree bears good fruit, but the rotten tree bears bad fruit.
From that time began Jesus to preach, and to say, Repent ye; for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
οὕτως πᾶν δένδρον ἀγαθὸν καρποὺς καλοὺς ποιεῖ, τὸ δὲ σαπρὸν δένδρον καρποὺς πονηροὺς ποιεῖ·
18
A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, nor can a rotten tree bear good fruit.
And walking by the sea of Galilee, he saw two brethren, Simon who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea; for they were fishers.
οὐ δύναται δένδρον ἀγαθὸν καρποὺς πονηροὺς ποιεῖν, οὐδὲ δένδρον σαπρὸν καρποὺς καλοὺς ποιεῖν.
19
Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
And he saith unto them, Come ye after me, and I will make you fishers of men.
πᾶν δένδρον μὴ ποιοῦν καρπὸν καλὸν ἐκκόπτεται καὶ εἰς πῦρ βάλλεται.
20
So then, by their fruits you will recognize them.
And they straightway left the nets, and followed him.
ἄρα γε ἀπὸ τῶν καρπῶν αὐτῶν ἐπιγνώσεσθε αὐτούς.
21
Not everyone who says to me, "Lord, Lord," will enter the kingdom of the heavens, but the one who does the will of my Father who is in the heavens.
And going on from thence he saw two other brethren, James the [son] of Zebedee, and John his brother, in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them.
Οὐ πᾶς ὁ λέγων μοι· Κύριε κύριε, εἰσελεύσεται εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἀλλ' ὁ ποιῶν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.
Translation Commentary Verse 21

ou pas ho legōn moi 'kyrie, kyrie' eiseleusetai eis tēn basileian tōn ouranōn, all' ho poiōn to thelēma tou patros mou tou en tois ouranois — 'not everyone who says to me Lord, Lord ... but the one who does the will of my Father in the heavens'. The Matthean-distinctive doing-the-will closing of the SM-ethic. The kingdom-of-the-heavens phrase per the Matthean redactional-pattern. See kingdom-of-heaven-basileia-tōn-ouranōn-mt-distinctive-cross-corpus-hebrew-malkhut-shamayim.

22
Many will say to me on that day, "Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, and in your name cast out demons, and in your name perform many mighty works?"
And they straightway left the boat and their father, and followed him.
πολλοὶ ἐροῦσίν μοι ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ· Κύριε κύριε, οὐ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι ἐπροφητεύσαμεν, καὶ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι δαιμόνια ἐξεβάλομεν, καὶ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι δυνάμεις πολλὰς ἐποιήσαμεν;
23
And then I will declare to them, "I never knew you; depart from me, you workers of lawlessness."
And Jesus went about in all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of disease and all manner of sickness among the people.
καὶ τότε ὁμολογήσω αὐτοῖς ὅτι Οὐδέποτε ἔγνων ὑμᾶς· ἀποχωρεῖτε ἀπ' ἐμοῦ οἱ ἐργαζόμενοι τὴν ἀνομίαν.
24
Therefore everyone who hears these words of mine and does them will be likened to a wise man who built his house upon the rock.
And the report of him went forth into all Syria: and they brought unto him all that were sick, holden with divers diseases and torments, possessed with demons, and epileptic, and palsied; and he healed them.
Πᾶς οὖν ὅστις ἀκούει μου τοὺς λόγους τούτους καὶ ποιεῖ αὐτούς, ὁμοιωθήσεται ἀνδρὶ φρονίμῳ, ὅστις ᾠκοδόμησεν αὐτοῦ τὴν οἰκίαν ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν.
Translation Commentary Verse 24

The two builders parable. pas oun hostis akouei mou tous logous toutous kai poiei autous — the SM's closing-parable contrasting hearer-and-doer with hearer-only. The petra (rock) vs ammos (sand) foundations + the storm-of-judgment imagery; the rock-foundation parallel echoes Isa 28:16 (the cornerstone-in-Zion).

25
And the rain came down, and the rivers came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it did not fall, for it had been founded upon the rock.
And there followed him great multitudes from Galilee and Decapolis and Jerusalem and Judaea and [from] beyond the Jordan.
καὶ κατέβη ἡ βροχὴ καὶ ἦλθον οἱ ποταμοὶ καὶ ἔπνευσαν οἱ ἄνεμοι καὶ προσέπεσαν τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἐκείνῃ, καὶ οὐκ ἔπεσεν, τεθεμελίωτο γὰρ ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν.
26
And everyone who hears these words of mine and does not do them will be likened to a foolish man who built his house upon the sand.
καὶ πᾶς ὁ ἀκούων μου τοὺς λόγους τούτους καὶ μὴ ποιῶν αὐτοὺς ὁμοιωθήσεται ἀνδρὶ μωρῷ, ὅστις ᾠκοδόμησεν αὐτοῦ τὴν οἰκίαν ἐπὶ τὴν ἄμμον.
27
And the rain came down, and the rivers came, and the winds blew, and struck against that house; and it fell — and great was its fall.
καὶ κατέβη ἡ βροχὴ καὶ ἦλθον οἱ ποταμοὶ καὶ ἔπνευσαν οἱ ἄνεμοι καὶ προσέκοψαν τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἐκείνῃ, καὶ ἔπεσεν, καὶ ἦν ἡ πτῶσις αὐτῆς μεγάλη.
28
And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished these words, the crowds were astonished at his teaching;
Καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοὺς λόγους τούτους, ἐξεπλήσσοντο οἱ ὄχλοι ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ·
Translation Commentary Verse 28

kai egeneto hote etelesen ho Iēsous tous logous toutous — 'and when Jesus finished these sayings'. The Matthean transition-formula closing the first of the five Matthean discourse-blocks (the SM is the first; the structure is generally treated as a Matthean Pentateuchal-typology with five discourse-blocks paralleling the five books of Moses). Davies-Allison ICC 1.725-727.

29
for he was teaching them as one having authority, and not as their scribes.
ἦν γὰρ διδάσκων αὐτοὺς ὡς ἐξουσίαν ἔχων καὶ οὐχ ὡς οἱ γραμματεῖς αὐτῶν.
Translation Commentary Verse 29

ēn gar didaskōn autous hōs exousian echōn, kai ouch hōs hoi grammateis — 'for he taught them as one having authority, and not as their scribes'. The Matthean Jesus' teaching-authority claim parallels the Mt 28:18 final authority-grant (edothē moi pasa exousia) — both deploy exousia. The polemical-comparison with the scribes is intra-Jewish, not anti-Jewish.

Chapter 13

Matthew 13 — The kingdom parables: Sower (Raëlian-canon panspermia site), Tares, Mustard Seed, Leaven, Hidden Treasure, Pearl, Net

1
On that day Jesus went out of the house and was sitting beside the sea.
And seeing the multitudes, he went up into the mountain: and when he had sat down, his disciples came unto him:
Ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ ἐξελθὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῆς οἰκίας ἐκάθητο παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν·
2
And great crowds were gathered to him, so that he got into a boat and sat down, and all the crowd stood on the shore.
and he opened his mouth and taught them, saying,
καὶ συνήχθησαν πρὸς αὐτὸν ὄχλοι πολλοί, ὥστε αὐτὸν εἰς πλοῖον ἐμβάντα καθῆσθαι, καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἐπὶ τὸν αἰγιαλὸν εἱστήκει.
3
And he spoke to them many things in parables, saying: "Behold, the sower went out to sow.
Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
καὶ ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς πολλὰ ἐν παραβολαῖς λέγων· Ἰδοὺ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ σπείρων τοῦ σπείρειν.
Translation Commentary Verse 3

The Parable of the Sower opens — one of the three major Raëlian-canon engagement sites in the Matthew translation. Idou exēlthen ho speirōn tou speirein — 'behold, the sower went out to sow' (generic-article ho speirōn = 'the sower', deliberate-typifying). Three reading-strata preserved without surface-adjudication: (1) the mainstream-Christian-traditional reception-of-the-Word reading; (2) the Jewish-historical-critical 1st-c. Galilean-Jewish agrarian-Sitz reading (Snodgrass 2008; Levine 2014); (3) the Raëlian-canon literal-soil-types-as-planet-types panspermia reading (Raël, The Role of Christ 1979). The WoH-Translation acknowledges-without-endorsing the Raëlian-canon citation per the Shi'ur Qomah / Qur'an / Exodus precedents. See parable-of-the-sower-mt-13-3-23-raelian-panspermia-canon-citation-cross-corpus-with-disavowals.

4
And as he sowed, some seeds fell beside the path, and the birds came and devoured them.
Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.
καὶ ἐν τῷ σπείρειν αὐτὸν ἃ μὲν ἔπεσεν παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν, καὶ ἐλθόντα τὰ πετεινὰ κατέφαγεν αὐτά.
Translation Commentary Verse 4

First soil-type: para tēn hodon (along the path). Standard reading: seed-eaten-by-birds, allegorized at v.19 as 'the evil one' snatching the word.

5
Others fell on rocky ground where they did not have much soil, and immediately they sprang up, because they had no depth of soil.
Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth.
ἄλλα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὰ πετρώδη ὅπου οὐκ εἶχεν γῆν πολλήν, καὶ εὐθέως ἐξανέτειλεν διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν βάθος γῆς.
Translation Commentary Verse 5

Second soil-type: epi ta petrōdē (on rocky-ground). Sprung-up-quickly-but-withered for lack of root.

6
But when the sun rose, they were scorched, and because they had no root, they withered away.
Blessed are they that hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled.
ἡλίου δὲ ἀνατείλαντος ἐκαυματίσθη καὶ διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν ῥίζαν ἐξηράνθη.
7
Others fell upon the thorns, and the thorns grew up and choked them.
Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.
ἄλλα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὰς ἀκάνθας, καὶ ἀνέβησαν αἱ ἄκανθαι καὶ ἀπέπνιξαν αὐτά.
Translation Commentary Verse 7

Third soil-type: epi tas akanthas (among thorns). Choked.

8
And others fell upon the good soil and bore fruit, some a hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty.
Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God.
ἄλλα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν τὴν καλὴν καὶ ἐδίδου καρπόν, ὃ μὲν ἑκατὸν ὃ δὲ ἑξήκοντα ὃ δὲ τριάκοντα.
Translation Commentary Verse 8

Fourth soil-type: epi tēn gēn tēn kalēn (on the good soil). Thirty/sixty/hundredfold yields — extraordinarily high; Palestinian average ~7-10:1 per agrarian-historical scholarship; Pliny NH 18.94-95 reports up to 100:1 only in exceptional Babylonian conditions. The hundredfold-yield echoes Gen 26:12 (Isaac's hundredfold harvest at Gerar).

9
Whoever has ears, let him hear."
Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called sons of God.
ὁ ἔχων ὦτα ἀκουέτω.
10
And the disciples came and said to him: "Why do you speak to them in parables?"
Blessed are they that have been persecuted for righteousness` sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
Καὶ προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Διὰ τί ἐν παραβολαῖς λαλεῖς αὐτοῖς;
Translation Commentary Verse 10

The parable-purpose intercalation (vv.10-17). The disciples ask why-Jesus-speaks-in-parables. Matthew's redactional pattern softens Mark's harsh hina-purpose-clause to a hoti-causal-clause at v.13 (see v.13 commentary).

11
And he answered and said to them: "To you it has been given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of the heavens, but to them it has not been given.
Blessed are ye when [men] shall reproach you, and persecute you, and say all manner of evil against you falsely, for my sake.
ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὅτι Ὑμῖν δέδοται γνῶναι τὰ μυστήρια τῆς βασιλείας τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἐκείνοις δὲ οὐ δέδοται.
Translation Commentary Verse 11

hymin dedotai gnōnai ta mystēria tēs basileias tōn ouranōn — 'to you it has been given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of the heavens'. The Matthean-distinctive kingdom-formula. mystēria (mysteries) — apocalyptic-revelation terminology rooted in Dan 2:18-19, 27-30 (the Daniel-mystery tradition). See kingdom-of-heaven-basileia-tōn-ouranōn-mt-distinctive-cross-corpus-hebrew-malkhut-shamayim.

12
For whoever has, to him more will be given, and he will have abundance; but whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken from him.
Rejoice, and be exceeding glad: for great is your reward in heaven: for so persecuted they the prophets that were before you.
ὅστις γὰρ ἔχει, δοθήσεται αὐτῷ καὶ περισσευθήσεται· ὅστις δὲ οὐκ ἔχει, καὶ ὃ ἔχει ἀρθήσεται ἀπ' αὐτοῦ.
13
This is why I speak to them in parables, because seeing they do not see, and hearing they do not hear, nor do they understand.
Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost its savor, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out and trodden under foot of men.
διὰ τοῦτο ἐν παραβολαῖς αὐτοῖς λαλῶ, ὅτι βλέποντες οὐ βλέπουσιν καὶ ἀκούοντες οὐκ ἀκούουσιν οὐδὲ συνίουσιν·
Translation Commentary Verse 13

Matthean softening of Mark's hina-clause. Mk 4:12 reads hina blepontes blepōsin ('in order that seeing they may not see' — the harsh predestinarian reading); Matthew 13:13 reads hoti blepontes ou blepousin ('because seeing they do not see' — the explanatory reading). The Matthean editorial-softening is part of the Matthean accommodation to a Jewish-Christian community-audience. Davies-Allison ICC 2.392-393.

14
And in them is being fulfilled the prophecy of Isaiah which says: "Hearing you will hear and not understand, and seeing you will see and not perceive.
Ye are the light of the world. A city set on a hill cannot be hid.
καὶ ἀναπληροῦται αὐτοῖς ἡ προφητεία Ἠσαΐου ἡ λέγουσα· Ἀκοῇ ἀκούσετε καὶ οὐ μὴ συνῆτε, καὶ βλέποντες βλέψετε καὶ οὐ μὴ ἴδητε.
Translation Commentary Verse 14

Isa 6:9-10 LXX citation. Matthew explicitly cites the Isa 6:9-10 LXX prophetic-hardening text. Lens-discipline: the Isa 6:9-10 citation is an INTERNAL-Israelite prophet's lament — NOT an ethnic indictment of Jewish unbelief, and must NOT be deployed in Christian-anti-Judaic supersessionist reading. Davies-Allison ICC 2.393-395; Levine-Brettler JANT 2017 ad loc.

15
