For the heart of this people has grown dull, and with their ears they barely heard, and they have closed their eyes — lest they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their heart and turn, and I should heal them."
Neither do [men] light a lamp, and put it under the bushel, but on the stand; and it shineth unto all that are in the house.
ἐπαχύνθη γὰρ ἡ καρδία τοῦ λαοῦ τούτου, καὶ τοῖς ὠσὶν βαρέως ἤκουσαν, καὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν ἐκάμμυσαν· μήποτε ἴδωσιν τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς καὶ τοῖς ὠσὶν ἀκούσωσιν καὶ τῇ καρδίᾳ συνῶσιν καὶ ἐπιστρέψωσιν, καὶ ἰάσομαι αὐτούς.
16
But blessed are your eyes, for they see, and your ears, for they hear.
Even so let your light shine before men; that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven.
ὑμῶν δὲ μακάριοι οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ ὅτι βλέπουσιν, καὶ τὰ ὦτα ὑμῶν ὅτι ἀκούουσιν.
17
For amen I say to you, many prophets and righteous people longed to see what you see and did not see it, and to hear what you hear and did not hear it.
Think not that I came to destroy the law or the prophets: I came not to destroy, but to fulfil.
ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πολλοὶ προφῆται καὶ δίκαιοι ἐπεθύμησαν ἰδεῖν ἃ βλέπετε καὶ οὐκ εἶδαν, καὶ ἀκοῦσαι ἃ ἀκούετε καὶ οὐκ ἤκουσαν.
18
You therefore, hear the parable of the sower.
For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass away, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass away from the law, till all things be accomplished.
Ὑμεῖς οὖν ἀκούσατε τὴν παραβολὴν τοῦ σπείραντος.
Translation Commentary Verse 18

The allegorical interpretation (vv.18-23). The Matthean Jesus' explicit interpretation of the four soil-types as the four reception-types of the Word. The interpretation is widely treated as either (a) substantially-authentic Jesus-tradition (Snodgrass 2008) or (b) early-community elaboration (Jeremias 1972).

19
When anyone hears the word of the kingdom and does not understand it, the evil one comes and snatches away what has been sown in his heart; this is the one sown beside the path.
Whosoever therefore shall break one of these least commandments, and shall teach men so, shall be called least in the kingdom of heaven: but whosoever shall do and teach them, he shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
παντὸς ἀκούοντος τὸν λόγον τῆς βασιλείας καὶ μὴ συνιέντος, ἔρχεται ὁ πονηρὸς καὶ ἁρπάζει τὸ ἐσπαρμένον ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ· οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ παρὰ τὴν ὁδὸν σπαρείς.
Translation Commentary Verse 19

ho ponēros — 'the evil one' (masculine-article; cf. Mt 6:13). The first-soil-type allegorical-meaning: the evil-one snatching the word.

20
And the one sown on the rocky ground — this is the one who hears the word and immediately receives it with joy,
For I say unto you, that except your righteousness shall exceed [the righteousness] of the scribes and Pharisees, ye shall in no wise enter into the kingdom of heaven.
ὁ δὲ ἐπὶ τὰ πετρώδη σπαρείς, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τὸν λόγον ἀκούων καὶ εὐθὺς μετὰ χαρᾶς λαμβάνων αὐτόν·
21
yet has no root in himself but is temporary, and when tribulation or persecution arises on account of the word, he immediately falls away.
Ye have heard that it was said to them of old time, Thou shalt not kill; and whosoever shall kill shall be in danger of the judgment:
οὐκ ἔχει δὲ ῥίζαν ἐν ἑαυτῷ ἀλλὰ πρόσκαιρός ἐστιν, γενομένης δὲ θλίψεως ἢ διωγμοῦ διὰ τὸν λόγον εὐθὺς σκανδαλίζεται.
22
And the one sown into the thorns — this is the one who hears the word, and the anxiety of the age and the deceitfulness of wealth choke the word, and he becomes unfruitful.
but I say unto you, that every one who is angry with his brother shall be in danger of the judgment; and whosoever shall say to his brother, Raca, shall be in danger of the council; and whosoever shall say, Thou fool, shall be in danger of the hell of fire.
ὁ δὲ εἰς τὰς ἀκάνθας σπαρείς, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τὸν λόγον ἀκούων καὶ ἡ μέριμνα τοῦ αἰῶνος καὶ ἡ ἀπάτη τοῦ πλούτου συμπνίγει τὸν λόγον, καὶ ἄκαρπος γίνεται.
Translation Commentary Verse 22

hē merimna tou aiōnos kai hē apatē tou ploutou — 'the anxiety of the age and the deceitfulness of wealth'. Cross-corpus to the Mt 6:25 mē merimnate anxiety-warning and the Mt 6:24 mamōnas wealth-warning — the SM-themes return in the parable's interpretation.

23
But the one sown on the good soil — this is the one who hears the word and understands it, who indeed bears fruit and yields, some a hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty.
If therefore thou art offering thy gift at the altar, and there rememberest that thy brother hath aught against thee,
ὁ δὲ ἐπὶ τὴν καλὴν γῆν σπαρείς, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τὸν λόγον ἀκούων καὶ συνιείς, ὃς δὴ καρποφορεῖ καὶ ποιεῖ ὃ μὲν ἑκατὸν ὃ δὲ ἑξήκοντα ὃ δὲ τριάκοντα.
24
He set before them another parable, saying: "The kingdom of the heavens has been likened to a man who sowed good seed in his field.
leave there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way, first be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift.
Ἄλλην παραβολὴν παρέθηκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ὡμοιώθη ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ σπείραντι καλὸν σπέρμα ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ αὐτοῦ.
Translation Commentary Verse 24

The Parable of the Tares. allēn parabolēn parethēken autois legōn; hōmoiōthē hē basileia tōn ouranōn anthrōpō speiranti kalon sperma en tō agrō autou — 'the kingdom of the heavens has been likened to a man who sowed good seed in his field'. The kingdom-similitude formula introduces the second of the seven Mt 13 kingdom-parables. Synoptic without parallel in Mark/Luke (uniquely Matthean).

25
But while the men slept, his enemy came and sowed darnel-weeds among the wheat and went away.
Agree with thine adversary quickly, while thou art with him in the way; lest haply the adversary deliver thee to the judge, and the judge deliver thee to the officer, and thou be cast into prison.
ἐν δὲ τῷ καθεύδειν τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἦλθεν αὐτοῦ ὁ ἐχθρὸς καὶ ἐπέσπειρεν ζιζάνια ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ σίτου καὶ ἀπῆλθεν.
26
But when the blade sprouted and bore fruit, then the darnel also appeared.
Verily I say unto thee, thou shalt by no means come out thence, till thou have paid the last farthing.
ὅτε δὲ ἐβλάστησεν ὁ χόρτος καὶ καρπὸν ἐποίησεν, τότε ἐφάνη καὶ τὰ ζιζάνια.
27
And the householder's slaves came and said to him: "Master, did you not sow good seed in your field? Where then has it got darnel?"
Ye have heard that it was said, Thou shalt not commit adultery:
προσελθόντες δὲ οἱ δοῦλοι τοῦ οἰκοδεσπότου εἶπον αὐτῷ· Κύριε, οὐχὶ καλὸν σπέρμα ἔσπειρας ἐν τῷ σῷ ἀγρῷ; πόθεν οὖν ἔχει ζιζάνια;
28
And he said to them: "An enemy has done this." And the slaves said to him: "Do you wish then that we go and gather them?"
but I say unto you, that every one that looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.
ὁ δὲ ἔφη αὐτοῖς· Ἐχθρὸς ἄνθρωπος τοῦτο ἐποίησεν. οἱ δὲ δοῦλοι λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Θέλεις οὖν ἀπελθόντες συλλέξωμεν αὐτά;
29
But he said: "No, lest in gathering the darnel you uproot the wheat together with it.
And if thy right eye causeth thee to stumble, pluck it out, and cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not thy whole body be cast into hell.
ὁ δέ φησιν· Οὔ, μήποτε συλλέγοντες τὰ ζιζάνια ἐκριζώσητε ἅμα αὐτοῖς τὸν σῖτον·
30
Let both grow together until the harvest; and at harvest time I will tell the reapers, 'Gather first the darnel and bind it into bundles to be burned, but gather the wheat into my barn.'"
And if thy right hand causeth thee to stumble, cut it off, and cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not thy whole body go into hell.
ἄφετε συναυξάνεσθαι ἀμφότερα μέχρι τοῦ θερισμοῦ· καὶ ἐν καιρῷ τοῦ θερισμοῦ ἐρῶ τοῖς θερισταῖς· Συλλέξατε πρῶτον τὰ ζιζάνια καὶ δήσατε αὐτὰ εἰς δέσμας πρὸς τὸ κατακαῦσαι αὐτά, τὸν δὲ σῖτον συναγάγετε εἰς τὴν ἀποθήκην μου.
31
He set before them another parable, saying: "The kingdom of the heavens is like a mustard seed that a man took and sowed in his field,
It was said also, Whosoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorcement:
Ἄλλην παραβολὴν παρέθηκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν κόκκῳ σινάπεως, ὃν λαβὼν ἄνθρωπος ἔσπειρεν ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ αὐτοῦ·
Translation Commentary Verse 31

The Parable of the Mustard Seed. kokkō sinapeōs — the mustard-seed parable. Cross-corpus to Dan 4:10-12 (Nebuchadnezzar's tree-vision) and Ezek 17:23 / Ezek 31:6 (the eschatological-tree-sheltering-birds image). The Matthean kingdom-formula again.

32
which is the smallest of all seeds, but when it has grown is greater than the garden plants and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the sky come and nest in its branches.
but I say unto you, that every one that putteth away his wife, saving for the cause of fornication, maketh her an adulteress: and whosoever shall marry her when she is put away committeth adultery.
ὃ μικρότερον μέν ἐστιν πάντων τῶν σπερμάτων, ὅταν δὲ αὐξηθῇ μεῖζον τῶν λαχάνων ἐστὶν καὶ γίνεται δένδρον, ὥστε ἐλθεῖν τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ κατασκηνοῦν ἐν τοῖς κλάδοις αὐτοῦ.
33
He spoke to them another parable: "The kingdom of the heavens is like leaven that a woman took and hid in three measures of flour, until it was all leavened."
Again, ye have heard that it was said to them of old time, Thou shalt not forswear thyself, but shalt perform unto the Lord thine oaths:
Ἄλλην παραβολὴν ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς· Ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ζύμῃ, ἣν λαβοῦσα γυνὴ ἐνέκρυψεν εἰς ἀλεύρου σάτα τρία ἕως οὗ ἐζυμώθη ὅλον.
Translation Commentary Verse 33

The Parable of the Leaven. Surprising: zymē (leaven) standardly carries negative-symbolism in Jewish-tradition (Ex 12:15-20 unleavened-bread; Mt 16:6 'beware of the leaven of the Pharisees'); the kingdom-as-leaven inverts the standard symbolism. Davies-Allison ICC 2.422-424.

34
All these things Jesus spoke to the crowds in parables, and without a parable he spoke nothing to them,
but I say unto you, swear not at all; neither by the heaven, for it is the throne of God;
ταῦτα πάντα ἐλάλησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν παραβολαῖς τοῖς ὄχλοις, καὶ χωρὶς παραβολῆς οὐδὲν ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς·
35
so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying: "I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter what has been hidden from the foundation."
nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of his feet; nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.
ὅπως πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος· Ἀνοίξω ἐν παραβολαῖς τὸ στόμα μου, ἐρεύξομαι κεκρυμμένα ἀπὸ καταβολῆς.
Translation Commentary Verse 35

Citation of Ps 78:2 LXX anoixō en parabolais to stoma mou ereuxomai kekrymmena apo katabolēs ('I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter what has been hidden from the foundation of the world'). The Matthean hina plērōthē fulfillment-formula again. Davies-Allison ICC 2.425-426.

36
Then leaving the crowds, he went into the house. And his disciples came to him, saying: "Explain to us the parable of the darnel of the field."
Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, for thou canst not make one hair white or black.
Τότε ἀφεὶς τοὺς ὄχλους ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν. καὶ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ λέγοντες· Διασάφησον ἡμῖν τὴν παραβολὴν τῶν ζιζανίων τοῦ ἀγροῦ.
Translation Commentary Verse 36

Transition to the indoor allegorical-interpretation of the Tares. The audience-shift (crowds → disciples) parallels the structure of the Sower-parable + interpretation.

37
And he answered and said: "The one who sows the good seed is the Son of Man.
But let your speech be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: and whatsoever is more than these is of the evil [one].
ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Ὁ σπείρων τὸ καλὸν σπέρμα ἐστὶν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου·
Translation Commentary Verse 37

ho speirōn to kalon sperma estin ho huios tou anthrōpou — 'the one sowing the good seed is the Son of Man'. The Son-of-Man identification (cf. Dan 7:13-14; Mt 25:31) — see son-of-man-bar-enash-dan-7-13-mt-cross-corpus.

38
The field is the world; the good seed — these are the sons of the kingdom; the darnel are the sons of the evil one,
Ye have heard that it was said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth:
ὁ δὲ ἀγρός ἐστιν ὁ κόσμος· τὸ δὲ καλὸν σπέρμα, οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ υἱοὶ τῆς βασιλείας· τὰ δὲ ζιζάνιά εἰσιν οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ πονηροῦ,
39
and the enemy who sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the consummation of the age, and the reapers are angels.
but I say unto you, resist not him that is evil: but whosoever smiteth thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also.
ὁ δὲ ἐχθρὸς ὁ σπείρας αὐτά ἐστιν ὁ διάβολος· ὁ δὲ θερισμὸς συντέλεια αἰῶνός ἐστιν, οἱ δὲ θερισταὶ ἄγγελοί εἰσιν.
40
Therefore as the darnel is gathered and burned with fire, so it shall be at the consummation of the age.
And if any man would go to law with thee, and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloak also.
ὥσπερ οὖν συλλέγεται τὰ ζιζάνια καὶ πυρὶ κατακαίεται, οὕτως ἔσται ἐν τῇ συντελείᾳ τοῦ αἰῶνος.
41
The Son of Man will send out his angels, and they will gather out of his kingdom all causes of offense and those who do lawlessness,
And whosoever shall compel thee to go one mile, go with him two.
ἀποστελεῖ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τοὺς ἀγγέλους αὐτοῦ, καὶ συλλέξουσιν ἐκ τῆς βασιλείας αὐτοῦ πάντα τὰ σκάνδαλα καὶ τοὺς ποιοῦντας τὴν ἀνομίαν,
Translation Commentary Verse 41

apostelei ho huios tou anthrōpou tous angelous autou — 'the Son of Man will send his angels'. Apocalyptic-judgment scene; the Son-of-Man-with-his-angels echoes Dan 7:10 + Mt 25:31. See son-of-man-bar-enash-dan-7-13-mt-cross-corpus.

42
and will throw them into the furnace of fire; there will be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.
Give to him that asketh thee, and from him that would borrow of thee turn not thou away.
καὶ βαλοῦσιν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν κάμινον τοῦ πυρός· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.
Translation Commentary Verse 42

tēn kaminon tou pyros; ekei estai ho klauthmos kai ho brygmos tōn odontōn — 'the furnace of fire; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth'. Apocalyptic-judgment imagery rooted in 1 Enoch 90:24-27 + Jub 24:30 + Dan 3:6 (Nebuchadnezzar's furnace). The 'weeping and gnashing of teeth' is a Matthean-distinctive formula (6x in Matthew + Lk 13:28).

43
Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Whoever has ears, let him hear.
Ye have heard that it was said, Thou shalt love thy neighbor, and hate thine enemy:
τότε οἱ δίκαιοι ἐκλάμψουσιν ὡς ὁ ἥλιος ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτῶν. ὁ ἔχων ὦτα ἀκουέτω.
44
The kingdom of the heavens is like treasure hidden in a field, which a man found and hid; and from joy over it he goes and sells all that he has and buys that field.
but I say unto you, love your enemies, and pray for them that persecute you;
Ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν θησαυρῷ κεκρυμμένῳ ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ, ὃν εὑρὼν ἄνθρωπος ἔκρυψεν, καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς χαρᾶς αὐτοῦ ὑπάγει καὶ πωλεῖ πάντα ὅσα ἔχει καὶ ἀγοράζει τὸν ἀγρὸν ἐκεῖνον.
Translation Commentary Verse 44

The Parable of the Hidden Treasure. Brief-vivid parable contrasting the discovery's joy and the all-in commitment.

45
Again, the kingdom of the heavens is like a merchant seeking fine pearls;
that ye may be sons of your Father who is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sendeth rain on the just and the unjust.
Πάλιν ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ ἐμπόρῳ ζητοῦντι καλοὺς μαργαρίτας·
Translation Commentary Verse 45

The Parable of the Pearl of Great Price. Parallel structure to the Hidden Treasure. The Matthean kingdom-formula again.

46
and having found one pearl of great value, he went and sold all that he had and bought it.
For if ye love them that love you, what reward have ye? do not even the publicans the same?
εὑρὼν δὲ ἕνα πολύτιμον μαργαρίτην ἀπελθὼν πέπρακεν πάντα ὅσα εἶχεν καὶ ἠγόρασεν αὐτόν.
47
Again, the kingdom of the heavens is like a dragnet cast into the sea and gathering of every kind,
And if ye salute your brethren only, what do ye more [than others?] do not even the Gentiles the same?
Πάλιν ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν σαγήνῃ βληθείσῃ εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ ἐκ παντὸς γένους συναγαγούσῃ·
Translation Commentary Verse 47

The Parable of the Net. The fishing-net + sorting-of-fish at the eschatological-judgment. The good-vs-bad sorting parallels the wheat-vs-tares structure of vv.24-30, 36-43.

48
which, when it was full, they drew up onto the shore, and sitting down they gathered the good into vessels but threw the bad away.
Ye therefore shall be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.
ἣν ὅτε ἐπληρώθη ἀναβιβάσαντες ἐπὶ τὸν αἰγιαλὸν καὶ καθίσαντες συνέλεξαν τὰ καλὰ εἰς ἄγγη, τὰ δὲ σαπρὰ ἔξω ἔβαλον.
49
So it shall be at the consummation of the age. The angels shall go out and separate the evil from among the righteous,
οὕτως ἔσται ἐν τῇ συντελείᾳ τοῦ αἰῶνος· ἐξελεύσονται οἱ ἄγγελοι καὶ ἀφοριοῦσιν τοὺς πονηροὺς ἐκ μέσου τῶν δικαίων
50
and shall throw them into the furnace of fire; there shall be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.
καὶ βαλοῦσιν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν κάμινον τοῦ πυρός· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.
51
Have you understood all these things?" They said to him, "Yes."
Συνήκατε ταῦτα πάντα; λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Ναί.
52
And he said to them: "Therefore every scribe who has been discipled into the kingdom of the heavens is like a householder who brings out of his treasure things new and old."
ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Διὰ τοῦτο πᾶς γραμματεὺς μαθητευθεὶς τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν ὅμοιός ἐστιν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδεσπότῃ ὅστις ἐκβάλλει ἐκ τοῦ θησαυροῦ αὐτοῦ καινὰ καὶ παλαιά.
Translation Commentary Verse 52

pas grammateus mathēteutheis tē basileia tōn ouranōn ... ekballei ek tou thēsaurou autou kaina kai palaia — 'every scribe trained for the kingdom of the heavens ... brings out from his treasure new things and old'. The Matthean self-identification of the trained-scribe (treasures-old-and-new = Hebrew Bible + Jesus-tradition). The Matthean closing of the kingdom-parables discourse-block. Davies-Allison ICC 2.445-447.

53
And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished these parables, he departed from there.
Καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὰς παραβολὰς ταύτας, μετῆρεν ἐκεῖθεν.
54
And coming into his native town, he taught them in their synagogue, so that they were astonished and said: "Where did this man get this wisdom and these mighty works?
καὶ ἐλθὼν εἰς τὴν πατρίδα αὐτοῦ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτοὺς ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ αὐτῶν, ὥστε ἐκπλήσσεσθαι αὐτοὺς καὶ λέγειν· Πόθεν τούτῳ ἡ σοφία αὕτη καὶ αἱ δυνάμεις;
Translation Commentary Verse 54

Transition to the Nazareth-rejection narrative. Cross-synoptic to Mk 6:1-6.

55
Is not this the carpenter's son? Is not his mother called Mary, and his brothers James and Joseph and Simon and Judas?
οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τοῦ τέκτονος υἱός; οὐχ ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ λέγεται Μαριὰμ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰωσὴφ καὶ Σίμων καὶ Ἰούδας;
56
And are not all his sisters with us? Where then did this man get all these things?"
καὶ αἱ ἀδελφαὶ αὐτοῦ οὐχὶ πᾶσαι πρὸς ἡμᾶς εἰσιν; πόθεν οὖν τούτῳ ταῦτα πάντα;
57
And they took offense at him. But Jesus said to them: "A prophet is not without honor, except in his native town and in his own household."
καὶ ἐσκανδαλίζοντο ἐν αὐτῷ. ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐκ ἔστιν προφήτης ἄτιμος εἰ μὴ ἐν τῇ πατρίδι καὶ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ.
Translation Commentary Verse 57

ouk estin prophētēs atimos ei mē en tē patridi autou — 'a prophet is not without honor except in his hometown'. The aphorism is preserved across the synoptic tradition (Mk 6:4; Lk 4:24; Jn 4:44) and in the Gospel of Thomas 31 — multiply-attested.

58
And he did not do many mighty works there, because of their unbelief.
καὶ οὐκ ἐποίησεν ἐκεῖ δυνάμεις πολλὰς διὰ τὴν ἀπιστίαν αὐτῶν.
Chapter 17

Matthew 17 — The Transfiguration + the demoniac boy + the temple-tax

1
And after six days Jesus took with him Peter and James and John his brother, and led them up onto a high mountain by themselves.
Take heed that ye do not your righteousness before men, to be seen of them: else ye have no reward with your Father who is in heaven.
Καὶ μεθ' ἡμέρας ἓξ παραλαμβάνει ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὸν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἀναφέρει αὐτοὺς εἰς ὄρος ὑψηλὸν κατ' ἰδίαν.
Translation Commentary Verse 1

The Transfiguration narrative opens. Kai meth' hēmeras hex paralambanei ho Iēsous ton Petron kai Iakōbon kai Iōannēn ... kai anaferei autous eis oros hypsēlon kat' idian — 'after six days, Jesus takes Peter, James, and John ... and brings them up to a high mountain by themselves'. The 'high mountain' (oros hypsēlon) traditionally identified as Mt Tabor (Origen onward) but more recently as Mt Hermon (2,814m, near Caesarea Philippi where Mt 16 sets the prior episode) per France NICNT 645. The mountain-as-revelation-site pattern continues from Mt 5:1 (SM) toward Mt 28:16 (Great Commission). See transfiguration-mt-17-1-9-elohim-manifest-in-glory-mosheh-eliyyahu-divine-presence-cross-corpus-with-disavowals and mountain-as-revelation-site-mt-cross-corpus-har-sinai-mount-sapunu.

2
And he was transfigured before them, and his face shone like the sun, and his garments became white as the light.
When therefore thou doest alms, sound not a trumpet before thee, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may have glory of men. Verily I say unto you, They have received their reward.
καὶ μετεμορφώθη ἔμπροσθεν αὐτῶν, καὶ ἔλαμψεν τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ὡς ὁ ἥλιος, τὰ δὲ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο λευκὰ ὡς τὸ φῶς.
Translation Commentary Verse 2

kai metemorphōthē emprosthen autōn, kai elampsen to prosōpon autou hōs ho hēlios, ta de himatia autou egeneto leuka hōs to phōs — 'and he was transfigured before them, and his face shone like the sun, and his clothes became white as the light'. The passive metemorphōthē preserves the divine-passive (the transfiguration is something done-to Jesus, not by him). The luminous-face-shining echoes Ex 34:29-35 (Moses' shining face after speaking with YHWH); the luminous-figure cross-corpus to Dan 10:6 LXX (the man-in-linen vision) and 1 Enoch 14:18-22 (the luminous-throne theophany). One of the three major Raëlian-canon engagement sites — acknowledgment-without-endorsement applied. See transfiguration-mt-17-1-9-elohim-manifest-in-glory-mosheh-eliyyahu-divine-presence-cross-corpus-with-disavowals.

3
And behold, there appeared to them Moses and Elijah, talking with him.
But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth:
καὶ ἰδοὺ ὤφθη αὐτοῖς Μωϋσῆς καὶ Ἠλίας συλλαλοῦντες μετ' αὐτοῦ.
Translation Commentary Verse 3

Mōysēs kai Hēlias syllalountes met' autou — 'Moses and Elijah talking with him'. Three readings of the Moses-Elijah pairing: (a) Law/Prophets witness-pair (mainstream Christian-tradition); (b) eschatological-returning figures (Moses-redivivus per Deut 18:15; Elijah-redivivus per Mal 4:5-6 + Mt 11:14); (c) bodily-translated figures (Moses' divinely-buried at Deut 34:5-6 + Assumption of Moses tradition; Elijah's 2 Kgs 2:11 fiery-chariot translation). Davies-Allison ICC 2.696-697.

4
And Peter answered and said to Jesus: "Lord, it is good for us to be here. If you wish, I will make here three tents: one for you, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah."
that thine alms may be in secret: and thy Father who seeth in secret shall recompense thee.
ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ· Κύριε, καλόν ἐστιν ἡμᾶς ὧδε εἶναι· εἰ θέλεις, ποιήσω ὧδε τρεῖς σκηνάς, σοὶ μίαν καὶ Μωϋσεῖ μίαν καὶ Ἠλίᾳ μίαν.
Translation Commentary Verse 4

Peter proposes three skēnas (tents/booths). Cross-corpus possibly to the Feast of Tabernacles / Sukkot (Lev 23:42-43) eschatological-dwelling tradition, or to the Ex 25:8-9 Tabernacle-pattern revealed on the mountain.

5
While he was still speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them, and behold, a voice from the cloud, saying: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; listen to him."
And when ye pray, ye shall not be as the hypocrites: for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have received their reward.
ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἰδοὺ νεφέλη φωτεινὴ ἐπεσκίασεν αὐτούς, καὶ ἰδοὺ φωνὴ ἐκ τῆς νεφέλης λέγουσα· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, ἐν ᾧ εὐδόκησα· ἀκούετε αὐτοῦ.
Translation Commentary Verse 5

Four-layered scriptural-allusion in the bath-qol voice. houtos estin ho huios mou ho agapētos, en hō eudokēsa; akouete autou — the divine-voice declaration combines: (i) Ps 2:7 LXX huios mou ei sy (Davidic-royal enthronement-psalm); (ii) Isa 42:1 LXX ho agapētos mou en hō eudokēsen hē psychē mou (Servant-of-YHWH first-servant-song); (iii) Deut 18:15 autou akousesthe (prophet-like-Moses prediction); (iv) Mt 3:17 baptism-voice intratextual-echo. The four-layered allusion compresses Davidic-messianic + Servant-figure + prophet-like-Moses + intratextual significations. The nephelē phōteinē (bright cloud) echoes Ex 24:15-18 Sinai-cloud-glory. See transfiguration-mt-17-1-9-elohim-manifest-in-glory-mosheh-eliyyahu-divine-presence-cross-corpus-with-disavowals.

6
And when the disciples heard, they fell on their faces and were exceedingly afraid.
But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thine inner chamber, and having shut thy door, pray to thy Father who is in secret, and thy Father who seeth in secret shall recompense thee.
καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ μαθηταὶ ἔπεσαν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον αὐτῶν καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν σφόδρα.
7
And Jesus came and touched them, saying: "Rise up, and do not be afraid."
And in praying use not vain repetitions, as the Gentiles do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking.
καὶ προσῆλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἁψάμενος αὐτῶν εἶπεν· Ἐγέρθητε καὶ μὴ φοβεῖσθε.
8
And lifting up their eyes, they saw no one except Jesus himself alone.
Be not therefore like unto them: for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him.
ἐπάραντες δὲ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν οὐδένα εἶδον εἰ μὴ αὐτὸν Ἰησοῦν μόνον.
9
And as they were coming down from the mountain, Jesus commanded them, saying: "Tell the vision to no one until the Son of Man is raised from the dead."
After this manner therefore pray ye. Our Father who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.
καὶ καταβαινόντων αὐτῶν ἐκ τοῦ ὄρους ἐνετείλατο αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων· Μηδενὶ εἴπητε τὸ ὅραμα ἕως οὗ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκ νεκρῶν ἐγερθῇ.
Translation Commentary Verse 9

tō huiō tou anthrōpou ek nekrōn egerthē — the Son-of-Man resurrection-prediction. The messianic-secret pattern: the disciples are commanded not-to-speak-of-the-vision until after the resurrection. See son-of-man-bar-enash-dan-7-13-mt-cross-corpus.

10
And his disciples asked him, saying: "Why then do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?"
Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done, as in heaven, so on earth.
καὶ ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ λέγοντες· Τί οὖν οἱ γραμματεῖς λέγουσιν ὅτι Ἠλίαν δεῖ ἐλθεῖν πρῶτον;
Translation Commentary Verse 10

Disciples' question about Elijah's coming. The Mal 4:5-6 Elijah-redivivus expectation; Mt 11:14 explicitly identifies the Baptist with Elijah-redivivus. Davies-Allison ICC 2.711-715.

11
And he answered and said: "Elijah indeed is coming and will restore all things;
Give us this day our daily bread.
ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Ἠλίας μὲν ἔρχεται καὶ ἀποκαταστήσει πάντα·
12
but I say to you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but did to him whatever they wished; so also the Son of Man is about to suffer at their hands."
And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.
λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι Ἠλίας ἤδη ἦλθεν, καὶ οὐκ ἐπέγνωσαν αὐτὸν ἀλλὰ ἐποίησαν ἐν αὐτῷ ὅσα ἠθέλησαν· οὕτως καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου μέλλει πάσχειν ὑπ' αὐτῶν.
Translation Commentary Verse 12

Hēlias ēdē ēlthen — Jesus identifies Elijah-already-come (the Baptist). The Son-of-Man passion-prediction integrated with the Elijah-typology. See son-of-man-bar-enash-dan-7-13-mt-cross-corpus.

13
Then the disciples understood that he had spoken to them about John the Baptist.
And bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil [one.]
τότε συνῆκαν οἱ μαθηταὶ ὅτι περὶ Ἰωάννου τοῦ βαπτιστοῦ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς.
14
And when they came to the crowd, a man approached him, kneeling before him,
For if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
Καὶ ἐλθόντων πρὸς τὸν ὄχλον προσῆλθεν αὐτῷ ἄνθρωπος γονυπετῶν αὐτὸν
Translation Commentary Verse 14

The demoniac-boy pericope opens. Synoptic-parallel: Mk 9:14-29; Lk 9:37-43. The Matthean form is shorter than the Markan.

15
and saying: "Lord, have mercy on my son, for he is moon-struck and suffers grievously; for often he falls into the fire and often into the water.
But if ye forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.
καὶ λέγων· Κύριε, ἐλέησόν μου τὸν υἱόν, ὅτι σεληνιάζεται καὶ κακῶς πάσχει· πολλάκις γὰρ πίπτει εἰς τὸ πῦρ καὶ πολλάκις εἰς τὸ ὕδωρ.
Translation Commentary Verse 15

selēniazetai — 'is moonstruck' (literally lunatic-from-Selēnē 'moon'). The ancient diagnosis of epilepsy / seizure-disorders attributed to lunar-influence. The Matthean term (vs the Markan pneuma alalon 'mute spirit') reflects different ancient medical-categories.

16
And I brought him to your disciples, but they could not heal him."
Moreover when ye fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may be seen of men to fast. Verily I say unto you, They have received their reward.
καὶ προσήνεγκα αὐτὸν τοῖς μαθηταῖς σου, καὶ οὐκ ἠδυνήθησαν αὐτὸν θεραπεῦσαι.
17
And Jesus answered and said: "O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I bear with you? Bring him here to me."
But thou, when thou fastest, anoint thy head, and wash thy face;
ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ὦ γενεὰ ἄπιστος καὶ διεστραμμένη, ἕως πότε μεθ' ὑμῶν ἔσομαι; ἕως πότε ἀνέξομαι ὑμῶν; φέρετέ μοι αὐτὸν ὧδε.
18
And Jesus rebuked it, and the demon came out of him; and the boy was healed from that hour.
that thou be not seen of men to fast, but of thy Father who is in secret: and thy Father, who seeth in secret, shall recompense thee.
καὶ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἀπ' αὐτοῦ τὸ δαιμόνιον· καὶ ἐθεραπεύθη ὁ παῖς ἀπὸ τῆς ὥρας ἐκείνης.
19
Then the disciples came to Jesus privately and said: "Why could we not cast it out?"
Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon the earth, where moth and rust consume, and where thieves break through and steal:
Τότε προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ τῷ Ἰησοῦ κατ' ἰδίαν εἶπον· Διὰ τί ἡμεῖς οὐκ ἠδυνήθημεν ἐκβαλεῖν αὐτό;
20
And he said to them: "Because of your little faith. For amen I say to you, if you have faith as a mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, 'Move from here to there,' and it will move; and nothing will be impossible for you.
but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth consume, and where thieves do not break through nor steal:
ὁ δὲ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Διὰ τὴν ὀλιγοπιστίαν ὑμῶν· ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐὰν ἔχητε πίστιν ὡς κόκκον σινάπεως, ἐρεῖτε τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ· Μετάβα ἔνθεν ἐκεῖ, καὶ μεταβήσεται, καὶ οὐδὲν ἀδυνατήσει ὑμῖν.
Translation Commentary Verse 20

ean echēte pistin hōs kokkon sinapeōs ... ereite tō orei toutō, metaba enthen ekei, kai metabēsetai — the mustard-seed-faith + move-the-mountain saying. Cross-synoptic Mt 21:21; Mk 11:23; 1 Cor 13:2. The mountain-imagery may activate the Matthean revelation-mountain pattern. See mountain-as-revelation-site-mt-cross-corpus-har-sinai-mount-sapunu.

21
[But this kind does not go out except by prayer and fasting.]
for where thy treasure is, there will thy heart be also.
[Τοῦτο δὲ τὸ γένος οὐκ ἐκπορεύεται εἰ μὴ ἐν προσευχῇ καὶ νηστείᾳ.]
22
And as they were gathering together in Galilee, Jesus said to them: "The Son of Man is about to be handed over into the hands of men,
The lamp of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.
Συστρεφομένων δὲ αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Μέλλει ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοσθαι εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων,
Translation Commentary Verse 22

Second passion-prediction. mellei ho huios tou anthrōpou paradidosthai eis cheiras anthrōpōn — 'the Son of Man is about to be handed over into human hands'. Part of the threefold Matthean passion-prediction series (Mt 16:21; 17:22-23; 20:18-19). The wordplay huios tou anthrōpou ... eis cheiras anthrōpōn (Son of Man into human hands) is preserved in Greek. See son-of-man-bar-enash-dan-7-13-mt-cross-corpus.

23
and they will kill him, and on the third day he will be raised." And they were exceedingly grieved.
But if thine eye be evil, thy whole body shall be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in thee be darkness, how great is the darkness!
καὶ ἀποκτενοῦσιν αὐτόν, καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἐγερθήσεται. καὶ ἐλυπήθησαν σφόδρα.
24
And when they came to Capernaum, the collectors of the two-drachma tax came to Peter and said: "Does not your teacher pay the two-drachma tax?"
No man can serve two masters; for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.
Ἐλθόντων δὲ αὐτῶν εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ προσῆλθον οἱ τὰ δίδραχμα λαμβάνοντες τῷ Πέτρῳ καὶ εἶπαν· Ὁ διδάσκαλος ὑμῶν οὐ τελεῖ τὰ δίδραχμα;
Translation Commentary Verse 24

The temple-tax pericope (vv.24-27). The didrachma — the two-drachma annual Temple-tax (Ex 30:11-16 the half-shekel atonement-tax tradition). The Matthean Jesus engages with the tax in a complex theological-political way: free-from-tax-as-sons but pays-it-not-to-offend. Uniquely Matthean.

25
He said, "Yes." And when he came into the house, Jesus anticipated him, saying: "What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth take tolls or tribute? From their own sons, or from strangers?"
Therefore I say unto you, be not anxious for your life, what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink; nor yet for your body, what ye shall put on. Is not the life more than the food, and the body than the raiment?
λέγει· Ναί. καὶ ἐλθόντα εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν προέφθασεν αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων· Τί σοι δοκεῖ, Σίμων; οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς ἀπὸ τίνων λαμβάνουσιν τέλη ἢ κῆνσον; ἀπὸ τῶν υἱῶν αὐτῶν ἢ ἀπὸ τῶν ἀλλοτρίων;
26
And when he said, "From strangers," Jesus said to him: "Then the sons are free.
Behold the birds of the heaven, that they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; and your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are not ye of much more value then they?
εἰπόντος δέ· Ἀπὸ τῶν ἀλλοτρίων, ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἄρα γε ἐλεύθεροί εἰσιν οἱ υἱοί.
27
But so that we may not offend them, go to the sea and cast a hook, and take the first fish that comes up; and when you have opened its mouth, you will find a stater. Take that and give it to them for me and yourself."
And which of you by being anxious can add one cubit unto the measure of his life?
ἵνα δὲ μὴ σκανδαλίσωμεν αὐτούς, πορευθεὶς εἰς θάλασσαν βάλε ἄγκιστρον καὶ τὸν ἀναβάντα πρῶτον ἰχθὺν ἆρον, καὶ ἀνοίξας τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ εὑρήσεις στατῆρα· ἐκεῖνον λαβὼν δὸς αὐτοῖς ἀντὶ ἐμοῦ καὶ σοῦ.
Translation Commentary Verse 27

stater — a four-drachma coin found in the fish's mouth. The fish-coin episode has been read as: (a) literal-miracle of provision; (b) parable-symbolic action; (c) folk-tale type. Davies-Allison ICC 2.745-746.

Chapter 25

Matthew 25 — Ten Virgins + Talents + Sheep and Goats (the final judgment)

1
Then the kingdom of the heavens will be likened to ten virgins, who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.
Judge not, that ye be not judged.
Τότε ὁμοιωθήσεται ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν δέκα παρθένοις, αἵτινες λαβοῦσαι τὰς λαμπάδας ἑαυτῶν ἐξῆλθον εἰς ὑπάντησιν τοῦ νυμφίου.
Translation Commentary Verse 1

The Ten Virgins parable opens. Tote homoiōthēsetai hē basileia tōn ouranōn deka parthenois — 'then the kingdom of the heavens will be likened to ten virgins'. The kingdom-similitude formula introduces the eschatological parable-pair (Ten Virgins + Talents) that closes the eschatological-discourse (Mt 23-25) before the Sheep-and-Goats final-judgment. The bridegroom-figure echoes the Hebrew Bible YHWH-as-bridegroom tradition (Hos 2; Isa 54:5; Jer 2:2). See kingdom-of-heaven-basileia-tōn-ouranōn-mt-distinctive-cross-corpus-hebrew-malkhut-shamayim.

2
And five of them were foolish, and five were prudent.
For with what judgment ye judge, ye shall be judged: and with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured unto you.
πέντε δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν ἦσαν μωραὶ καὶ πέντε φρόνιμοι.
3
For the foolish, when they took their lamps, took no oil with them;
And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother`s eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye?
αἱ γὰρ μωραὶ λαβοῦσαι τὰς λαμπάδας αὐτῶν οὐκ ἔλαβον μεθ' ἑαυτῶν ἔλαιον·
4
but the prudent took oil in their flasks along with their lamps.
Or how wilt thou say to thy brother, Let me cast out the mote out of thine eye; and lo, the beam is in thine own eye?
αἱ δὲ φρόνιμοι ἔλαβον ἔλαιον ἐν τοῖς ἀγγείοις μετὰ τῶν λαμπάδων ἑαυτῶν.
5
And while the bridegroom was delayed, they all became drowsy and slept.
Thou hypocrite, cast out first the beam out of thine own eye; and then shalt thou see clearly to cast out the mote out of thy brother`s eye.
χρονίζοντος δὲ τοῦ νυμφίου ἐνύσταξαν πᾶσαι καὶ ἐκάθευδον.
6
But at midnight there came a cry: "Behold, the bridegroom! Come out to meet him."
Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast your pearls before the swine, lest haply they trample them under their feet, and turn and rend you.
μέσης δὲ νυκτὸς κραυγὴ γέγονεν· Ἰδοὺ ὁ νυμφίος, ἐξέρχεσθε εἰς ἀπάντησιν.
7
Then all those virgins rose and trimmed their lamps.
Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you:
τότε ἠγέρθησαν πᾶσαι αἱ παρθένοι ἐκεῖναι καὶ ἐκόσμησαν τὰς λαμπάδας ἑαυτῶν.
8
And the foolish said to the prudent, "Give us some of your oil, for our lamps are going out."
for every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened.
αἱ δὲ μωραὶ ταῖς φρονίμοις εἶπαν· Δότε ἡμῖν ἐκ τοῦ ἐλαίου ὑμῶν, ὅτι αἱ λαμπάδες ἡμῶν σβέννυνται.
9
But the prudent answered, saying, "There will not be enough for us and for you. Go rather to those who sell and buy for yourselves."
Or what man is there of you, who, if his son shall ask him for a loaf, will give him a stone;
ἀπεκρίθησαν δὲ αἱ φρόνιμοι λέγουσαι· Μήποτε οὐ μὴ ἀρκέσῃ ἡμῖν καὶ ὑμῖν· πορεύεσθε μᾶλλον πρὸς τοὺς πωλοῦντας καὶ ἀγοράσατε ἑαυταῖς.
10
And while they were going off to buy, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready went in with him to the wedding feast, and the door was shut.
or if he shall ask for a fish, will give him a serpent?
ἀπερχομένων δὲ αὐτῶν ἀγοράσαι ἦλθεν ὁ νυμφίος, καὶ αἱ ἕτοιμοι εἰσῆλθον μετ' αὐτοῦ εἰς τοὺς γάμους, καὶ ἐκλείσθη ἡ θύρα.
11
Later, the other virgins also came, saying, "Lord, lord, open to us."
If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father who is in heaven give good things to them that ask him?
ὕστερον δὲ ἔρχονται καὶ αἱ λοιπαὶ παρθένοι λέγουσαι· Κύριε κύριε, ἄνοιξον ἡμῖν.
12
But he answered, saying, "Amen I say to you, I do not know you."
All things therefore whatsoever ye would that men should do unto you, even so do ye also unto them: for this is the law and the prophets.
ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐκ οἶδα ὑμᾶς.
13
Keep watch, therefore, for you know neither the day nor the hour.
Enter ye in by the narrow gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many are they that enter in thereby.
γρηγορεῖτε οὖν, ὅτι οὐκ οἴδατε τὴν ἡμέραν οὐδὲ τὴν ὥραν.
Translation Commentary Verse 13

grēgoreite oun, hoti ouk oidate tēn hēmeran oude tēn hōran — 'keep watch, therefore, for you do not know the day or the hour'. The eschatological-vigilance theme; Mt 24:42, 44, 50; Mk 13:33; the grēgoreite watchword.

14
For it is just as when a man going on a journey called his own servants and entrusted to them his possessions.
For narrow is the gate, and straitened the way, that leadeth unto life, and few are they that find it.
Ὥσπερ γὰρ ἄνθρωπος ἀποδημῶν ἐκάλεσεν τοὺς ἰδίους δούλους καὶ παρέδωκεν αὐτοῖς τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ,
Translation Commentary Verse 14

The Talents parable opens. Synoptic-parallel: Lk 19:11-27 (the more-elaborate Lukan minas-parable). The talanton — a large weight-measure of silver, ~6,000 denarii or ~20 years of laborer-wages. The parable's accounting-figures are deliberately enormous.

15
And to one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one, to each according to his own ability; and he went on his journey. At once
Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep`s clothing, but inwardly are ravening wolves.
καὶ ᾧ μὲν ἔδωκεν πέντε τάλαντα ᾧ δὲ δύο ᾧ δὲ ἕν, ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὴν ἰδίαν δύναμιν, καὶ ἀπεδήμησεν. εὐθέως
16
the one who had received the five talents went and traded with them and gained another five.
By their fruits ye shall know them. Do [men] gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles?
πορευθεὶς ὁ τὰ πέντε τάλαντα λαβὼν ἠργάσατο ἐν αὐτοῖς καὶ ἐκέρδησεν ἄλλα πέντε·
17
Likewise the one who had the two gained another two.
Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but the corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit.
ὡσαύτως ὁ τὰ δύο ἐκέρδησεν ἄλλα δύο·
18
But the one who had received the one went off and dug in the ground and hid his master's silver.
A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit.
ὁ δὲ τὸ ἓν λαβὼν ἀπελθὼν ὤρυξεν γῆν καὶ ἔκρυψεν τὸ ἀργύριον τοῦ κυρίου αὐτοῦ.
19
Now after a long time the master of those servants came and settled accounts with them.
Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire.
μετὰ δὲ πολὺν χρόνον ἔρχεται ὁ κύριος τῶν δούλων ἐκείνων καὶ συναίρει λόγον μετ' αὐτῶν
20
And the one who had received the five talents came forward and brought another five talents, saying, "Master, you entrusted to me five talents; see, I have gained another five talents."
Therefore by their fruits ye shall know them.
καὶ προσελθὼν ὁ τὰ πέντε τάλαντα λαβὼν προσήνεγκεν ἄλλα πέντε τάλαντα λέγων· Κύριε, πέντε τάλαντά μοι παρέδωκας· ἴδε ἄλλα πέντε τάλαντα ἐκέρδησα.
21
His master said to him, "Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a few things; I will set you over many. Enter into the joy of your master."
Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father who is in heaven.
ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ· Εὖ, δοῦλε ἀγαθὲ καὶ πιστέ, ἐπὶ ὀλίγα ἦς πιστός, ἐπὶ πολλῶν σε καταστήσω· εἴσελθε εἰς τὴν χαρὰν τοῦ κυρίου σου.
Translation Commentary Verse 21

eu, doule agathe kai piste ... eiselthe eis tēn charan tou kyriou sou — 'well done, good and faithful servant ... enter into the joy of your lord'. The reward-formula; cross-corpus to Jewish-apocalyptic reward-of-the-righteous (1 Enoch 39:3-14; T. Levi 18; 4 Ezra 7).

22
The one who had received the two talents also came forward and said, "Master, you entrusted to me two talents; see, I have gained another two talents."
Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy by thy name, and by thy name cast out demons, and by thy name do many mighty works?
προσελθὼν δὲ καὶ ὁ τὰ δύο τάλαντα εἶπεν· Κύριε, δύο τάλαντά μοι παρέδωκας· ἴδε ἄλλα δύο τάλαντα ἐκέρδησα.
23
His master said to him, "Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a few things; I will set you over many. Enter into the joy of your master."
And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.
ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ· Εὖ, δοῦλε ἀγαθὲ καὶ πιστέ, ἐπὶ ὀλίγα ἦς πιστός, ἐπὶ πολλῶν σε καταστήσω· εἴσελθε εἰς τὴν χαρὰν τοῦ κυρίου σου.
24
Then the one who had received the one talent also came forward and said, "Master, I knew you to be a hard man, reaping where you did not sow and gathering where you did not scatter;
Every one therefore that heareth these words of mine, and doeth them, shall be likened unto a wise man, who built his house upon the rock:
προσελθὼν δὲ καὶ ὁ τὸ ἓν τάλαντον εἰληφὼς εἶπεν· Κύριε, ἔγνων σε ὅτι σκληρὸς εἶ ἄνθρωπος, θερίζων ὅπου οὐκ ἔσπειρας καὶ συνάγων ὅθεν οὐ διεσκόρπισας·
25
and being afraid, I went and hid your talent in the ground. See, you have what is yours."
and the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and if fell not: for it was founded upon the rock.
καὶ φοβηθεὶς ἀπελθὼν ἔκρυψα τὸ τάλαντόν σου ἐν τῇ γῇ· ἴδε ἔχεις τὸ σόν.
26
But his master answered him, saying, "Wicked and slothful servant! You knew that I reap where I did not sow and gather where I did not scatter?
And every one that heareth these words of mine, and doeth them not, shall be likened unto a foolish man, who built his house upon the sand:
ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Πονηρὲ δοῦλε καὶ ὀκνηρέ, ᾔδεις ὅτι θερίζω ὅπου οὐκ ἔσπειρα καὶ συνάγω ὅθεν οὐ διεσκόρπισα;
27
You ought, then, to have put my silver with the bankers, and on my coming I would have received back what was mine with interest.
and the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and smote upon that house; and it fell: and great was the fall thereof.
ἔδει σε οὖν βαλεῖν τὰ ἀργύριά μου τοῖς τραπεζίταις, καὶ ἐλθὼν ἐγὼ ἐκομισάμην ἂν τὸ ἐμὸν σὺν τόκῳ.
28
Take therefore the talent from him and give it to the one who has the ten talents.
And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished these words, the multitudes were astonished at his teaching:
ἄρατε οὖν ἀπ' αὐτοῦ τὸ τάλαντον καὶ δότε τῷ ἔχοντι τὰ δέκα τάλαντα·
29
For to everyone who has, more will be given, and he will have abundance; but from the one who has not, even what he has will be taken away.
for he taught them as [one] having authority, and not as their scribes.
τῷ γὰρ ἔχοντι παντὶ δοθήσεται καὶ περισσευθήσεται· τοῦ δὲ μὴ ἔχοντος καὶ ὃ ἔχει ἀρθήσεται ἀπ' αὐτοῦ.
30
And cast the useless servant into the outer darkness; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth."
καὶ τὸν ἀχρεῖον δοῦλον ἐκβάλετε εἰς τὸ σκότος τὸ ἐξώτερον· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.
Translation Commentary Verse 30

to skotos to exōteron; ekei estai ho klauthmos kai ho brygmos tōn odontōn — 'the outer darkness; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth'. The Matthean-distinctive apocalyptic-judgment formula (also at Mt 8:12; 13:42; 13:50; 22:13; 24:51).

31
When the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the angels with him, then he will sit on the throne of his glory.
Ὅταν δὲ ἔλθῃ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐν τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ καὶ πάντες οἱ ἄγγελοι μετ' αὐτοῦ, τότε καθίσει ἐπὶ θρόνου δόξης αὐτοῦ·
Translation Commentary Verse 31

The Sheep-and-Goats Final Judgment opens. Hotan de elthē ho huios tou anthrōpou en tē doxē autou kai pantes hoi angeloi met' autou, tote kathisei epi thronou doxēs autou — 'when the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the angels with him, then he will sit on his glorious throne'. Direct appropriation of Dan 7:13-14 LXX: the thronos doxēs echoes Dan 7:9 enthronement; angels-attending echoes Dan 7:10; universal-judgment role echoes Dan 7:14. See son-of-man-bar-enash-dan-7-13-mt-cross-corpus and sheep-and-goats-mt-25-31-46-adelphōn-mou-tōn-elachistōn-three-readings-gray-cross-corpus.

32
And all the nations will be gathered before him, and he will separate them one from another as the shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.
καὶ συναχθήσονται ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, καὶ ἀφορίσει αὐτοὺς ἀπ' ἀλλήλων, ὥσπερ ὁ ποιμὴν ἀφορίζει τὰ πρόβατα ἀπὸ τῶν ἐρίφων,
Translation Commentary Verse 32

synachthēsontai emprosthen autou panta ta ethnē — 'all the nations will be gathered before him'. panta ta ethnē admits both the universalist 'all peoples including Israel' and the strict 'all the Gentile-nations' readings (Hare/Harrington 1975 vs Meier 1977). Cross-corpus to Joel 3:11-12 (the eschatological-judgment-of-the-nations).

33
And he will set the sheep at his right hand, and the goats at the left.
καὶ στήσει τὰ μὲν πρόβατα ἐκ δεξιῶν αὐτοῦ τὰ δὲ ἐρίφια ἐξ εὐωνύμων.
Translation Commentary Verse 33

Sheep-and-goats sorting-image. Cross-corpus to Ezek 34:17-22 (the eschatological-sorting-of-the-flock prophecy).

34
Then the king will say to those at his right hand, "Come, you who are blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.
τότε ἐρεῖ ὁ βασιλεὺς τοῖς ἐκ δεξιῶν αὐτοῦ· Δεῦτε, οἱ εὐλογημένοι τοῦ πατρός μου, κληρονομήσατε τὴν ἡτοιμασμένην ὑμῖν βασιλείαν ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου.
Translation Commentary Verse 34

deute hoi eulogēmenoi tou patros mou, klēronomēsate tēn hētoimasmenēn hymin basileian apo katabolēs kosmou — 'come, you blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world'. The kingdom-as-inheritance from-the-foundation-of-the-world echoes Jewish-apocalyptic pre-existent-creation themes (4 Ezra 8:52; 2 Bar 4:3).

35
For I was hungry and you gave me food; I was thirsty and you gave me drink; I was a stranger and you took me in;
ἐπείνασα γὰρ καὶ ἐδώκατέ μοι φαγεῖν, ἐδίψησα καὶ ἐποτίσατέ με, ξένος ἤμην καὶ συνηγάγετέ με,
Translation Commentary Verse 35

The six-fold acts-of-mercy list (vv.35-36). Hungry-fed / thirsty-given-drink / stranger-welcomed / naked-clothed / sick-visited / imprisoned-visited. Cross-corpus to Isa 58:6-10 (the prophetic critique-of-fasting + acts-of-mercy program); Job 22:6-7; T. Iss. 7:5; T. Jos. 1:5-7; m.Sotah 14a (the rabbinic gemilut ḥasadim tradition). The Matthean Final-Judgment criterion is rooted in Jewish-mercy tradition.

36
naked and you clothed me; I was sick and you visited me; I was in prison and you came to me."
γυμνὸς καὶ περιεβάλετέ με, ἠσθένησα καὶ ἐπεσκέψασθέ με, ἐν φυλακῇ ἤμην καὶ ἤλθατε πρός με.
37
Then the righteous will answer him, saying, "Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you drink?
τότε ἀποκριθήσονται αὐτῷ οἱ δίκαιοι λέγοντες· Κύριε, πότε σε εἴδομεν πεινῶντα καὶ ἐθρέψαμεν, ἢ διψῶντα καὶ ἐποτίσαμεν;
38
And when did we see you a stranger and take you in, or naked and clothe you?
πότε δέ σε εἴδομεν ξένον καὶ συνηγάγομεν, ἢ γυμνὸν καὶ περιεβάλομεν;
39
And when did we see you sick or in prison and come to you?"
πότε δέ σε εἴδομεν ἀσθενοῦντα ἢ ἐν φυλακῇ καὶ ἤλθομεν πρός σε;
40
And the king will answer them, saying, "Amen I say to you, inasmuch as you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me."
καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ βασιλεὺς ἐρεῖ αὐτοῖς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐφ' ὅσον ἐποιήσατε ἑνὶ τούτων τῶν ἀδελφῶν μου τῶν ἐλαχίστων, ἐμοὶ ἐποιήσατε.
Translation Commentary Verse 40

The central crux. eph' hoson epoiēsate heni toutōn tōn adelphōn mou tōn elachistōn, emoi epoiēsate — 'inasmuch as you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me'. The adelphōn mou tōn elachistōn identification-question is the load-bearing interpretive-site. Gray 1989 identifies three reading-strata: (1) universalist (= all suffering humanity); (2) restricted-Christian-missionary (= the disciple-band, cf. Mt 10:42); (3) restricted-Christian-brethren (= the suffering-poor-among-Christians). All three readings have substantial-textual warrant; the philological data does not by itself decide. The WoH-Translation preserves the literal 'brothers' rendering and documents all three readings in sheep-and-goats-mt-25-31-46-adelphōn-mou-tōn-elachistōn-three-readings-gray-cross-corpus. Note the textual-asymmetry with v.45 (which lacks adelphōn mou) — see overlay entry adelphōn-mou-presence-absence-asymmetry-mt-25-40-vs-25-45-gray.

41
Then he will say also to those at the left, "Depart from me, you cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.
Τότε ἐρεῖ καὶ τοῖς ἐξ εὐωνύμων· Πορεύεσθε ἀπ' ἐμοῦ κατηραμένοι εἰς τὸ πῦρ τὸ αἰώνιον τὸ ἡτοιμασμένον τῷ διαβόλῳ καὶ τοῖς ἀγγέλοις αὐτοῦ.
Translation Commentary Verse 41

to pyr to aiōnion to hētoimasmenon tō diabolō kai tois angelois autou — 'the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels'. aiōnios — the philological-breadth question: 'endless-eternal' (KJV/RSV/NRSV/NIV) vs 'age-pertaining' (Hart 2017 et al.). Cross-corpus to 1 Enoch 90:24-27 (apocalyptic fire-of-judgment for the fallen-angels); Jub 24:30; Rev 20:10, 14-15. The WoH-Translation preserves 'eternal' per the dominant English-tradition convention and documents the breadth in aiōnios-mt-25-41-46-eternal-vs-age-pertaining-cross-corpus + overlay aionios-eternal-vs-age-pertaining-translation-convention.

42
For I was hungry and you gave me no food; I was thirsty and you gave me no drink;
ἐπείνασα γὰρ καὶ οὐκ ἐδώκατέ μοι φαγεῖν, ἐδίψησα καὶ οὐκ ἐποτίσατέ με,
43
I was a stranger and you did not take me in; naked and you did not clothe me; sick and in prison and you did not visit me."
ξένος ἤμην καὶ οὐ συνηγάγετέ με, γυμνὸς καὶ οὐ περιεβάλετέ με, ἀσθενὴς καὶ ἐν φυλακῇ καὶ οὐκ ἐπεσκέψασθέ με.
44
Then they also will answer, saying, "Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison and did not serve you?"
τότε ἀποκριθήσονται καὶ αὐτοὶ λέγοντες· Κύριε, πότε σε εἴδομεν πεινῶντα ἢ διψῶντα ἢ ξένον ἢ γυμνὸν ἢ ἀσθενῆ ἢ ἐν φυλακῇ καὶ οὐ διηκονήσαμέν σοι;
45
Then he will answer them, saying, "Amen I say to you, inasmuch as you did not do it to one of the least of these, neither did you do it to me."
τότε ἀποκριθήσεται αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐφ' ὅσον οὐκ ἐποιήσατε ἑνὶ τούτων τῶν ἐλαχίστων, οὐδὲ ἐμοὶ ἐποιήσατε.
Translation Commentary Verse 45

Textual asymmetry. eph' hoson ouk epoiēsate heni toutōn tōn elachistōn, oude emoi epoiēsate — 'inasmuch as you did it not to one of the least of these, you did it not to me'. NOTE: v.45 LACKS adelphōn mou present at v.40. The asymmetry is preserved per Gray 1989. Implications for the universalist-vs-restricted reading-debate are documented in overlay entry adelphōn-mou-presence-absence-asymmetry-mt-25-40-vs-25-45-gray.

46
And these will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.
καὶ ἀπελεύσονται οὗτοι εἰς κόλασιν αἰώνιον, οἱ δὲ δίκαιοι εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
Translation Commentary Verse 46

kai apeleusontai houtoi eis kolasin aiōnion, hoi de dikaioi eis zōēn aiōnion — 'and these will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life'. The Matthean parallel-structure kolasin aiōnion / zōēn aiōnion. The parallel-structure argument: if aiōnion in 'eternal life' means 'endless-eternal', then aiōnion in 'eternal punishment' must equally. The conditionalist counter-argument: parallelism does not require identical-semantic-content. The WoH-Translation preserves 'eternal' on the surface; see aiōnios-mt-25-41-46-eternal-vs-age-pertaining-cross-corpus.

Chapter 28

Matthew 28 — The Resurrection + the Great Commission

1
Now after the Sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb.
And when he was come down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him.
Ὀψὲ δὲ σαββάτων, τῇ ἐπιφωσκούσῃ εἰς μίαν σαββάτων, ἦλθεν Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ ἡ ἄλλη Μαρία θεωρῆσαι τὸν τάφον.
Translation Commentary Verse 1

The Resurrection-narrative opens. Opse de sabbatōn, tē epiphōskousē eis mian sabbatōn — 'after the sabbath, as the first day of the week was dawning'. The temporal-marker establishes the early-Sunday-morning setting; the Christian first-day-of-the-week (kyriakē hēmera) tradition derives from this Synoptic dating. Mary Magdalene and 'the other Mary' (Mary mother of James + Joses per Mt 27:56) are the first-witnesses — preserved across the Synoptic-tradition (Mk 16:1; Lk 24:10; Jn 20:1).

2
And behold, there was a great earthquake; for an angel of the Lord, having come down from heaven, came and rolled away the stone, and sat upon it.
And behold, there came to him a leper and worshipped him, saying, Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.
καὶ ἰδοὺ σεισμὸς ἐγένετο μέγας· ἄγγελος γὰρ κυρίου καταβὰς ἐξ οὐρανοῦ καὶ προσελθὼν ἀπεκύλισεν τὸν λίθον καὶ ἐκάθητο ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ.
Translation Commentary Verse 2

seismos egeneto megas; angelos gar kyriou katabas ex ouranou — 'a great earthquake occurred; for an angel of the Lord descending from heaven'. The Matthean-distinctive earthquake (paralleling the Mt 27:51-54 crucifixion-earthquake) is unique to Matthew. The angelos kyriou katabas ex ouranou — calques the LXX malʾakh YHWH descending; the Matthean angelophanic-pattern from Mt 1:20 + 2:13 + 2:19 + 2:22 (the four Joseph dream-revelations) continues.

3
His appearance was like lightning, and his garment white as snow.
And he stretched forth his hand, and touched him, saying, I will; be thou made clean. And straightway his leprosy was cleansed.
ἦν δὲ ἡ εἰδέα αὐτοῦ ὡς ἀστραπὴ καὶ τὸ ἔνδυμα αὐτοῦ λευκὸν ὡς χιών.
Translation Commentary Verse 3

hē eidea autou hōs astrapē kai to endyma autou leukon hōs chiōn — 'his appearance like lightning and his clothing white as snow'. The luminous-angelic description draws on Dan 7:9 LXX (the Ancient-of-Days enthronement: clothing-white-as-snow) + Dan 10:6 LXX (the man-in-linen luminous-vision). The same vocabulary describes the Transfiguration at Mt 17:2 — Matthean intratextual-echo. See transfiguration-mt-17-1-9-elohim-manifest-in-glory-mosheh-eliyyahu-divine-presence-cross-corpus-with-disavowals.

4
And for fear of him the guards trembled and became like dead men.
And Jesus saith unto him, See thou tell no man; but go, show thyself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.
ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ φόβου αὐτοῦ ἐσείσθησαν οἱ τηροῦντες καὶ ἐγενήθησαν ὡς νεκροί.
5
But the angel answered and said to the women, "Do not be afraid, for I know that you are seeking Jesus the crucified.
And when he was entered into Capernaum, there came unto him a centurion, beseeching him,
ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ ἄγγελος εἶπεν ταῖς γυναιξίν· Μὴ φοβεῖσθε ὑμεῖς, οἶδα γὰρ ὅτι Ἰησοῦν τὸν ἐσταυρωμένον ζητεῖτε·
Translation Commentary Verse 5

mē phobeisthe hymeis — 'do not be afraid'. The angelic-reassurance formula (Gen 15:1; Lk 1:13, 30; Mt 1:20). Cross-corpus to the divine-encounter-fear-formula across the Hebrew Bible.

6
He is not here, for he has been raised, just as he said. Come, see the place where he lay.
and saying, Lord, my servant lieth in the house sick of the palsy, grievously tormented.
οὐκ ἔστιν ὧδε, ἠγέρθη γὰρ καθὼς εἶπεν· δεῦτε ἴδετε τὸν τόπον ὅπου ἔκειτο.
Translation Commentary Verse 6

ouk estin hōde, ēgerthē gar kathōs eipen — 'he is not here, for he is risen as he said'. The empty-tomb proclamation; the passive ēgerthē (he was raised) preserves the divine-passive (God raised him, not Jesus raised-himself). Cross-synoptic-parallel.

7
And go quickly and tell his disciples that he has been raised from the dead, and behold, he goes before you into Galilee; there you will see him. Behold, I have told you."
And he saith unto him, I will come and heal him.
καὶ ταχὺ πορευθεῖσαι εἴπατε τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ὅτι Ἠγέρθη ἀπὸ τῶν νεκρῶν, καὶ ἰδοὺ προάγει ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν, ἐκεῖ αὐτὸν ὄψεσθε· ἰδοὺ εἶπον ὑμῖν.
8
And they went away quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy, and ran to bring word to his disciples.
And the centurion answered and said, Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof; but only say the word, and my servant shall be healed.
καὶ ἀπελθοῦσαι ταχὺ ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου μετὰ φόβου καὶ χαρᾶς μεγάλης ἔδραμον ἀπαγγεῖλαι τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ.
9
And behold, Jesus met them, saying, "Greetings." And they came up and took hold of his feet and worshipped him.
For I also am a man under authority, having under myself soldiers: and I say to this one, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth it.
καὶ ἰδοὺ Ἰησοῦς ὑπήντησεν αὐταῖς λέγων· Χαίρετε· αἱ δὲ προσελθοῦσαι ἐκράτησαν αὐτοῦ τοὺς πόδας καὶ προσεκύνησαν αὐτῷ.
Translation Commentary Verse 9

kai idou Iēsous hypēntēsen autais — 'and behold, Jesus met them'. The Matthean-distinctive Jerusalem-area resurrection-appearance to the women (Mk 16:8 ends without resurrection-appearances; Lk 24 + Jn 20 have varied appearance-traditions).

10
Then Jesus said to them, "Do not be afraid. Go and tell my brothers to go into Galilee, and there they will see me."
And when Jesus heard it, he marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.
τότε λέγει αὐταῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Μὴ φοβεῖσθε· ὑπάγετε ἀπαγγείλατε τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς μου ἵνα ἀπέλθωσιν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν, κἀκεῖ με ὄψονται.
Translation Commentary Verse 10

hypagete apangeilate tois adelphois mou hina apelthōsin eis tēn Galilaian, kakei me opsontai — 'go and tell my brothers to depart for Galilee, and there they will see me'. The Galilee-appearance instruction sets up the Mt 28:16-20 Great Commission scene. adelphois mou — Jesus' brothers = the disciples (paralleling Mt 12:48-50; relevant to the Mt 25:40 adelphōn mou identification-question — see sheep-and-goats-mt-25-31-46-adelphōn-mou-tōn-elachistōn-three-readings-gray-cross-corpus).

11
While they were going, behold, some of the guard came into the city and reported to the chief priests everything that had happened.
And I say unto you, that many shall come from the east and the west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven:
Πορευομένων δὲ αὐτῶν ἰδού τινες τῆς κουστωδίας ἐλθόντες εἰς τὴν πόλιν ἀπήγγειλαν τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν ἅπαντα τὰ γενόμενα.
Translation Commentary Verse 11

The guard-at-the-tomb apologetic (vv.11-15) — uniquely Matthean. Addresses the Jewish-Christian polemical-context: the body-stolen-by-disciples counter-narrative (preserved in Justin's Dialogue with Trypho 108 and in later rabbinic anti-Christian polemical-tradition). The pericope is generally treated as a 2nd-half-of-1st-c. Matthean-community apologetic-narrative. Davies-Allison ICC 3.666-672.

12
And when they had assembled with the elders and taken counsel together, they gave a sufficient sum of silver to the soldiers,
but the sons of the kingdom shall be cast forth into the outer darkness: there shall be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.
καὶ συναχθέντες μετὰ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων συμβούλιόν τε λαβόντες ἀργύρια ἱκανὰ ἔδωκαν τοῖς στρατιώταις
13
saying, "Tell them, 'His disciples came by night and stole him while we were sleeping.'
And Jesus said unto the centurion, Go thy way; as thou hast believed, [so] be it done unto thee. And the servant was healed in that hour.
λέγοντες· Εἴπατε ὅτι Οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ νυκτὸς ἐλθόντες ἔκλεψαν αὐτὸν ἡμῶν κοιμωμένων·
14
And if this comes to the governor's ears, we will satisfy him and keep you out of trouble."
And when Jesus was come into Peter`s house, he saw his wife`s mother lying sick of a fever.
καὶ ἐὰν ἀκουσθῇ τοῦτο ἐπὶ τοῦ ἡγεμόνος, ἡμεῖς πείσομεν αὐτὸν καὶ ὑμᾶς ἀμερίμνους ποιήσομεν.
15
So they took the silver and did as they had been taught. And this story has been spread among Jews to this day.
And he touched her hand, and the fever left her; and she arose, and ministered unto him.
οἱ δὲ λαβόντες τὰ ἀργύρια ἐποίησαν ὡς ἐδιδάχθησαν. καὶ διεφημίσθη ὁ λόγος οὗτος παρὰ Ἰουδαίοις μέχρι τῆς σήμερον ἡμέρας.
16
Now the eleven disciples went into Galilee, to the mountain to which Jesus had directed them.
And when even was come, they brought unto him many possessed with demons: and he cast out the spirits with a word, and healed all that were sick:
Οἱ δὲ ἕνδεκα μαθηταὶ ἐπορεύθησαν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν εἰς τὸ ὄρος οὗ ἐτάξατο αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς,
Translation Commentary Verse 16

The Great Commission scene opens. Hoi de hendeka mathētai eporeuthēsan eis tēn Galilaian eis to oros hou etaxato autois ho Iēsous — 'the eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had appointed them'. The mountain-as-revelation-site pattern closes the Matthean Gospel (parallel to Mt 5:1 SM-mountain + Mt 17:1 Transfiguration-mountain). See mountain-as-revelation-site-mt-cross-corpus-har-sinai-mount-sapunu. The eleven (hendeka) — Matthias not-yet-elected (cf. Acts 1:15-26).

17
And when they saw him, they worshipped him; but some doubted.
that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying: Himself took our infirmities, and bare our diseases.
καὶ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν προσεκύνησαν, οἱ δὲ ἐδίστασαν.
Translation Commentary Verse 17

hoi de edistasan — 'but some doubted'. The Matthean honesty: the resurrection-appearance is met with mixed-response, not unanimous-confession. The historical-honesty parallel to Mk 16:8 (the women's fear-and-flight) + Lk 24:11 (the disciples' disbelief) + Jn 20:25 (Thomas's doubt).

18
And Jesus came up and spoke to them, saying, "All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.
Now when Jesus saw great multitudes about him, he gave commandments to depart unto the other side.
καὶ προσελθὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ἐδόθη μοι πᾶσα ἐξουσία ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς.
Translation Commentary Verse 18

edothē moi pasa exousia en ouranō kai epi gēs — 'all authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth'. Direct appropriation of Dan 7:13-14 LXX kai edothē autō exousia ... kai pasa tou kosmou ho oikoumenē — the Son-of-Man-enthronement authority-grant. The Risen Jesus' authority-claim explicitly draws on the Dan 7 Son-of-Man tradition. See son-of-man-bar-enash-dan-7-13-mt-cross-corpus and great-commission-mt-28-19-20-trinitarian-baptismal-formula-conybeare-hypothesis-cross-corpus-with-disavowals.

19
Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
And there came a scribe, and said unto him, Teacher, I will follow thee whithersoever thou goest.
πορευθέντες οὖν μαθητεύσατε πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, βαπτίζοντες αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος,
Translation Commentary Verse 19

The Great Commission proper. poreuthentes oun mathēteusate panta ta ethnē, baptizontes autous eis to onoma tou patros kai tou huiou kai tou hagiou pneumatos — 'going therefore, make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit'. The panta ta ethnē resolves the prior Matthean Israel-only mission-restrictions (Mt 10:5-6; 15:24). The trinitarian baptismal formula is preserved in ALL extant Greek manuscripts including Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + Alexandrinus + the early papyri. The Conybeare 1901 hypothesis that the Eusebian pre-Nicene shorter form en tō onomati mou represents an earlier reading is documented as one scholarly position without adjudication. Three reading-strata preserved (mainstream Christian-tradition / Conybeare-hypothesis / Raëlian-canon Elohim-Son-Spirit reading). Lens-discipline operational disavowals explicitly reject (i) Sitchin / Anunnaki engineered-Elohim-craft pre-resolution, (ii) orientalist / colonialist Great-Commission misreadings, (iii) Raëlian-canon Elohim-Son-Spirit-triad pre-resolution. See great-commission-mt-28-19-20-trinitarian-baptismal-formula-conybeare-hypothesis-cross-corpus-with-disavowals.

20
teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you; and behold, I am with you always, to the consummation of the age.
And Jesus saith unto him, The foxes have holes, and the birds of the heaven [have] nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head.
διδάσκοντες αὐτοὺς τηρεῖν πάντα ὅσα ἐνετειλάμην ὑμῖν· καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ μεθ' ὑμῶν εἰμι πάσας τὰς ἡμέρας ἕως τῆς συντελείας τοῦ αἰῶνος.
Translation Commentary Verse 20

idou egō meth' hymōn eimi pasas tas hēmeras heōs tēs synteleias tou aiōnos — 'behold, I am with you all the days until the end of the age'. The Matthean Emmanuel-inclusio closes with the abiding-presence promise that echoes Mt 1:23 Meth' hēmōn ho theos ('God with us'). The inclusio is the central Matthean structural-theological framing (Kupp 1996). See emmanuel-frame-inclusio-mt-1-23-mt-28-20-divine-presence-cross-corpus-kupp. The synteleia tou aiōnos (end of the age) eschatological-formula — aiōn as age-pertaining (echoing the Mt 25:41/46 aiōnios usage). The Matthean Gospel closes with the eschatological-presence promise.

Contents

    Wheel of Heaven is an open, multilingual reading of the ancient world's creation traditions — Raëlian, biblical, Mesopotamian, and others — through a single working hypothesis: that the beings called Elohim were a small advanced human civilization that came here, designed life on Earth, and left a record in the religious texts. The reading runs across twelve ages of the precessional cycle, from the project's beginning twenty-two thousand years ago to the present age of disclosure and into the long future the next Great Year is opening. The site is free, source-aware, and built so the work can be checked.
